- **A predictor's default figure pools its counted forecasts across every
  non-revoked window, and the window becomes the by-protocol cut; declared
  2026-10-11.** A **reading-rule declaration** made ahead of its
  implementation, because its evidentiary value is its date. It moves no
  digest, no constant, no window and no membership: `uv run fedcourts
  process-digest --all` at this commit prints `proc-v9` and the six digests the
  `proc-v9` entry above tabulates, and `COUNTING_WINDOWS` is unchanged. It
  changes which figure over the already-counted cells is the headline and
  which is the breakdown. It amends two bullets of the 2026-09-26 entry:
  - "No ranked or headline figure pools across windows" is replaced by the
    pooled default below;
  - "Engines are compared only over events, not spans" keeps its event
    grain, but loses its "each from one named window" condition and its
    split-event exclusion. Its selection disclosures still stand: a
    successor's entry states the split-event count and, per engine, how many
    of its counted events hold a failed or missing earlier-window attempt.
    Their reason, that the events an engine finishes late are the hard cases,
    survives pooling, which brings those events into the paired figure.

  It also replaces, once implemented, the cross-engine reading the `proc-v9`
  entry above draws for after its label: ranks restarting within each window
  label, and the two refusing builds. Every other bullet of the 2026-09-26
  entry stands.

  **Why now.** Protocol changes are to be promoted as they arrive, so a Term
  may run through many windows per predictor. Under a rule that keys every
  headline on (predictor, window), each figure would then be a small sample,
  and the record a reader wants, how well this predictor has forecast, would
  exist only as a sum nobody publishes. The maintainer set this direction on
  2026-10-10. That cadence, not any window's board, is the ground for the
  rule.

  **The declaration.**

  - **The default figure is the predictor's forward track record.** For each
    predictor, the default frozen-scope figure (its board entry and stage
    blocks, its claim scores, its ops score rows and tool-usage segments) is
    computed over every counted cell in every window no revocation has
    de-counted. Membership is unchanged: one counted forecast per (predictor,
    event), the earliest window's, graded under the gate of the window that
    opened it. Pooling adds no cell the window rule does not already count
    and drops none.
  - **A pooled figure is computed over the pooled cells**, exactly as a single
    window's figure is computed over its cells: the same per-cell terms, the
    same per-cell base-rate anchors for skill, the same weighting. It is not
    an average of window figures.
  - **No Term or trailing bound.** The default spans every non-revoked
    window. A figure bounded by Term, date or a trailing run of windows is a
    cut, named with its bound, over the same membership.
  - **Every pooled figure states its composition.** Beside the value it lists
    each window it pools, by label, with its `n`. The per-(predictor, window)
    figure is kept and published as the **by-protocol cut**, beside the
    default rather than as the headline.
  - **The by-protocol cut is a comparison over different events.** Two
    windows of one predictor share no event, and a successor's events are
    those the closed window did not reach, a selected population. So a move
    from one window's cut to the next answers "did the change help?" only as
    a comparison over different event sets, flagged as such, never as a
    measurement of improvement.
  - **Engines are compared over paired events, with no window restriction.**
    A cross-engine comparison is read over the events on which every compared
    engine holds a counted cell, whichever windows those cells come from.
    Pooling lets each engine's event set drift with its own history, so the
    pooled entries side by side are not a comparison; the paired reading
    carries it. The complete grid becomes that paired-event figure, and it
    lists, per engine, the windows its paired cells come from with their
    `n`. The board's paired set is the intersection over every engine it
    ranks, and the rank is read off it, never off pooled entries over
    differing event sets. Adding or retiring an engine moves that
    intersection and so the ranks; the figure names the engines it pairs.
    A pairwise comparison is its own figure over the two engines' paired
    events and is never read as the board's rank.
  - **Harness boundaries under an unchanged digest are composition, not
    silence.** A change the freeze record dates that moves what a cell reads
    without moving a digest, such as the predict-cell hide that `proc-v9`'s
    promotion carries into the codex and gemini windows, cuts nothing out of
    the pooled default or the paired figure. Both carry, per engine, the `n`
    on each side of every such dated boundary, so a paired event that joins
    a cell from before the hide to one from after it is visible as such.
    A dated change to the cohort cutoff or to `cut_kind` is listed the same
    way.
  - **Judge-dependent figures carry a per-rubric breakdown.** Every figure
    computed from an evaluator's judgment depends on the evaluate prompt, so
    a pool across evaluator digests mixes judge rubrics. That family
    includes `mean_reasoning_quality`, the `big_case` tau-b, the
    judge-validation tau-b, `evaluator_agreement` and the semantic grades.
    Each lists the evaluator digests it spans with their `n`, and its
    **per-rubric reading is the claimable figure**. The value pooled across
    more than one evaluator digest is published beside it as coverage, never
    as a claim or a rank key, as the reading rules already say for a
    `reasoning_quality` mean that spans a rubric boundary.
  - **Pooling windows licenses no other pooling.** Stratum, stage and moment,
    salience band and version, scoring baseline, claim-set version and every
    other boundary registered elsewhere still cut the pooled figure exactly
    as they cut a window's.
  - **Revocation remains the only de-count**, for a stated defect, under the
    2026-09-26 entry's rule. A revoked window leaves the pooled figure.
    Nothing else removes a window from it: not a successor that improves on
    it, and not its own figure.
  - **`release-sensitivity` and `semantic-summary` pool with the breakdown
    instead of refusing** once a predictor holds graded cells in two windows.
  - **The pool spans model changes too.** A window opened because a
    predictor's model changed pools into that predictor's default like a
    window opened by a prompt or harness change, with the by-protocol cut
    naming each window's model: `claude-baseline`'s `proc-v8` window
    (`claude-fable-5-1`) and its `proc-v9` window (`claude-opus-5-5`) are one
    pooled record and two cuts. The alternative, a model change as a hard
    series break, was the open question when this direction was set; the
    maintainer decided it on 2026-10-11, in favour of pooling with the
    breakdown.

  **The objection, and why the pool is still honest.** The 2026-09-26 entry
  held that a new model under an unchanged `predictor_id` is a different
  forecaster, so an engine's cells on either side of a closed window are two
  series. The pooled default instead treats a `predictor_id` as one forecaster
  whose process evolves and whose record accrues, model changes included. The
  pooled figure stays an honest out-of-sample record for four reasons:
  - every counted forecast was committed and stamped inside a window
    registered before its outcome existed, so each is out-of-sample however
    the process changed between forecasts;
  - one forecast per event, the earliest window's, means no later protocol or
    model can replace a forecast once made, or be swapped in on an event after
    its outcome is visible;
  - windows open at registered instants and close only at a successor's, and
    a revocation needs a defect shown from committed artifacts without
    reference to any outcome. A revocation may come after outcomes are
    visible, but only on that standard and disclosing the resolved slice, so
    no window can be removed from the record because of its results;
  - what pooling gives up, that the figure describes one fixed process, the
    by-protocol cut restores, and the composition beside every pooled value
    says how much of the record each process contributed.

  What the pool does not license: reading the pooled figure as a property of
  the current process or model; reading a change between cuts as
  improvement; reading two engines' pooled entries as a comparison.

  The implementation is fixed by this text and is **not tuned on `proc-v9`

- **The pooled default's implementation choices, settled ahead of the first
  `proc-v9` `claude-baseline` grading, 2026-10-11.** A **reading-rule**
  entry that completes the 2026-10-11 pooled-rule declaration above. That
  entry fixed the rule and left a few mechanical choices to its
  implementation, on the condition that any choice settled after a `proc-v9`
  `claude-baseline` grading lands is disclosed together with the outcomes
  visible when it was made. This entry settles them before then. It moves
  no digest, no constant, no window and no membership: `uv run fedcourts
  process-digest --all` prints the same `proc-v9` digests, and
  `COUNTING_WINDOWS` is unchanged. Nothing it names exists in code yet. "The
  implementation" below means the change that builds the declaration.

  **Composition and the by-protocol cut.**

  - **Composition is always listed.** Every pooled figure lists the windows it
    pools, each with its `n`. A window is named by its own label and opening
    instant, the window the cell's digest and stamp fall in, never by the
    stamp's label. A `codex-baseline` cell stamped `proc-v9` inside codex's
    `proc-v8` window is listed under `proc-v8`. The listing appears even when
    a figure pools a single window. Today's per-window listings, the board's
    per-combination `complete_grids` and the `windows` lists, appear only
    under more than one label. The default figure does not keep that
    omission, because the declaration asks for composition beside every
    pooled value.
  - **The by-protocol cut** is the per-(predictor, window) figure the boards
    publish today. It is listed beside the pooled default and never ranked.

  **The paired events and the rank.**

  - **The ranked set.** It holds every predictor that has a counting window
    neither closed nor revoked, and at least one **counted**, forward cert cell
    at the board's ranked moment carrying both an accuracy and a Brier score.
    - **Listed unranked.** A predictor whose every window is closed or revoked
      is retired: it keeps its pooled entry and its cut, but is not ranked.
      Taking a predictor off the roster therefore goes through a re-bless that
      closes its window.
    - **No floor.** There is no minimum cell count to join, so one engine with
      one cell can shrink the paired set to one event. The paired `n` is
      printed beside every rank so that this is visible.
  - **The paired events.** An event is paired where every engine in the ranked
    set holds such a counted cell on it, from any window. Pairing does not
    look at the salience band: the rank's keys use no band anchor, so a band
    condition would only shrink and select the set.
    - **Per-band readings.** For these, each paired event is assigned the band
      key of its earliest counted cell by harness clock. The count of paired
      events whose engines' cells carry different band keys is published
      beside the per-band split. Such mismatches are expected to cluster on
      events whose band rose between engines' runs: relists and CVSGs, the
      higher-grant events.
  - **The rank key.** Ranks are read off each ranked engine's aggregate over
    the paired events: forward accuracy, highest first; then forward mean
    Brier, lowest first; then `predictor_id`. There is no retrospective
    tie-break, because retrospective cells are not paired.
    - **Edge cases.** With one ranked engine, its paired events are its own
      qualifying events, and it ranks 1. With an empty paired set, no entry is
      ranked and the rank is null.
  - **Window ownership.** Each counting window records the predictor whose
    digest it counts, so retirement is read per predictor. A window naming no
    predictor retires nobody.
  - **The all-versions build** has no windows, so it has no open-window
    condition. It ranks every predictor that holds a qualifying cell, over the
    same paired construction. It is never the headline.
  - **The non-cert stage blocks** carry the same construction over their own
    events, unranked. Each block's engine set is the engines that hold a
    counted forward cell carrying accuracy and Brier in that block, with the
    same open-window condition.
  - **The selection disclosures stay in the record.** These are the
    split-event count and the per-engine count of counted events holding a
    failed or missing earlier-window attempt. They stay with
    `successor-disclosures`, which the declaration keeps. The paired figure
    states its own pairing losses, meaning each engine's qualifying events
    that are not paired, but does not repeat those disclosures.
    - **The uniform engine deadline.** That disclosure is also where the
      2026-10-08 change is read. The change moves which codex cells finish,
      and so which events reach the paired set.
  - **Applied to the visible `proc-v8` slice,** these choices reproduce the
    published board. At `metrics/leaderboard.json` on `main` (refreshed at
    `3f3ca14f4`):
    - each of the three predictors holds one window and 97 scored events;
    - the per-band complete grid sums to 97, with no band mismatch;
    - the forward accuracies are distinct, so the order claude, codex,
      gemini is unchanged without the retrospective tie-break.

  **Harness boundaries.**

  - **What they are.** These are the dated changes that the declaration's
    *harness boundaries* bullet names. Each moves what a predict cell reads,
    or the cohort cutoff or `cut_kind`, under an unchanged predictor digest.
    The declaration made them composition rather than cuts. Accordingly, the
    "may not be pooled" clauses of the conditioning entries listed below now
    read as composition for the pooled default and the paired figure. They
    still cut any figure that reads a boundary's own effect.
  - **The side test.** A cell's side of a boundary is the one those entries
    registered. A stamped cell is after the change if the carrying merge
    commit is an ancestor of, or equal to, its `process_version.pipeline_sha`.
    The instant below is for display only. A cell with no `pipeline_sha` is
    counted on neither side, and its number is listed.
  - **The registry.** The implementation registers each boundary in code with
    its carrying commit, that commit's committer time, the predictors it

  - **How the counts read.** Each pooled entry and each engine in the paired

  - **The last three, for `claude-baseline`.** Merge `6460e9306` registers

    Their own cautions still stand:

  - **Later boundaries.** A later change of this class is added to the

  **Judge-dependent figures.**

  - **The rubric.** A grading's rubric is its `evaluator_id` together with the
    `process_version.digest` on the evaluation's harness stamp.
  - **Per-judge figures** are `mean_reasoning_quality` and the ops
    reasoning-quality quantiles. Each is read per (evaluator, digest).
  - **Panel figures** are the `big_case` tau-b against the panel mean, the
    judge-validation tau-b, `evaluator_agreement` and the semantic per-grader
    agreement. The last two are leave-one-out: each judge is read against its
    peers, so both are properties of the panel.
    - **Rubric signature.** A panel figure is read per rubric signature: the
      sorted set of (evaluator, digest) pairs its reads come from. It is named
      by the evaluate labels that blessed those digests, and the label never
      partitions anything.
    - **Panel points.** A panel point belongs to a signature's reading only if
      every read in it carries one of that signature's pairs. The point must
      also meet the pooled figure's own minimum within that signature: a
      predictor-against-panel point needs at least one panel read, and a
      leave-one-out point needs the judge and at least one peer. A point whose
      reads span two signatures belongs to no per-rubric reading. It still
      counts in the pooled coverage value.
  - **What each figure lists.** Every judge-dependent figure lists the
    (evaluator, digest) pairs it spans, each with its `n`.

  **The other surfaces.**

  - **Pooled default plus cut.** The claim scores, the ops score rows and the
    tool-usage segments get the same pooled default with composition, with
    the per-window form as the cut. The tool-usage segments are keyed on
    engine, mode, stage and moment.
  - **`release-sensitivity`** projects the pooled entries and the paired
    figure.
  - **`semantic-summary`** pools, listing composition and rubric signatures.
  - **Refusals.** The frozen-scope pass stops refusing a predictor whose cells
    span two windows. It still refuses two windows of one predictor that share
    a label.

- **A respondent's brief "in partial support of" the petitioner no longer
  dates the briefed merits moment, 2026-10-11.** A **conditioning** entry in
  two classes at once: it moves the date the registered **briefed** merits
  moment opens at (the *provisioning cutoff*), and it moves which entries the
  merits arms of the document selector read (*what the pipeline provisions*).
  The exclusion that keeps a party siding with its opponent out of that side's
  merits filings (`merits_signals._NOT_THE_RESPONDENT_MERITS_FILING_RE`, and
  its petitioner mirror) read "in support of" and "supporting"; it now reads
  "in partial support of" as well. Before the change, a docket on which a
  respondent filed "Brief of respondent(s) … in partial support of
  petitioner" on the petitioner's schedule had its briefed moment opened, and
  its respondent brief filled, from a petitioner-side-only record. Observed
  on 25-1017 (`scotus/73281056`), a multi-respondent docket:
  `merits_brief_filed` reads `2026-08-28`, the day three aligned respondents
  filed (the United States and the legislative leaders "in support", the State
  of Arizona "in partial support", the last of which alone opened the
  moment), while the adverse respondents' briefs are due `2026-10-13`.

  What reads the two exclusions, and so moves: `respondent_brief_date` (the
  briefed moment's date, on the respondent side only, since nothing dates a
  petitioner-side moment); all four merits arms of the selector, the brief
  and the reply on each side (`is_respondent_merits_brief_document`,
  `is_petitioner_merits_brief`, and both `is_*_merits_reply` predicates); the
  consolidated member's borrow, whose side filter reads the same four
  predicates; and the `document-backfill` gap floor, which measures a docket
  against those arms. In each, an entry "in partial support of" the other side
  is no longer read as that side's own merits filing. What stays: the reply
  arms' motion and application exclusion, the cert-stage arms, and the
  staged-text contact scrub.

  No prompt byte and no registry field moves, so no digest moves:
  `uv run fedcourts process-digest --all` at this commit prints `proc-v9` and
  the six digests `605201bd…` (claude-baseline), `70fee158…`
  (codex-baseline), `a9033e56…` (gemini-baseline), `167b7d71…`
  (claude-judge), `18a76b93…` (codex-judge) and `22558044…` (gemini-judge),
  identical with and without the change.

  **A harness boundary under the 2026-10-11 pooled rule.** The change moves
  what a predict cell reads under unchanged digests, inside claude's `proc-v9`
  window and codex's and gemini's still-open `proc-v8` windows. Under the
  pooled-rule declaration's *harness boundaries* bullet it is composition,
  not a cut: the pooled default and the paired figure keep both sides and list
  each engine's `n` before and after. It cuts only a figure that reads its own
  effect, such as a briefed-moment lead time or a per-moment document-coverage
  reading. The cells that can read it are the briefed merits moment's and any
  later post-grant cell's on an affected docket. A cert-stage cell predates
  the grant, and the merits grant moment is cut at the grant, so neither reads
  a merits brief.
  - **The registry row.** The boundary is `merits-brief-partial-support`:
    `HarnessBoundary("merits-brief-partial-support", <carrying promotion merge
    hash>, <its committer time, UTC>, None, "granted dockets", gradual=True)`.
    It applies to every predictor, and it is gradual because both halves reach
    a docket only through a later poll or fetch. Its carrying merge exists only
    once the promotion merges, so the row joins
    `process_version.HARNESS_BOUNDARIES` in the post-promotion fill PR that
    completes this entry's placeholders, as the registry's first eleven rows
    did. A leaderboard built on `main` between the promotion and that fill
    omits this boundary's listing. That loses composition only, never a cut or
    a score. The fill PR targets `staging`, so the omission lasts until the
    promotion that carries the fill, not only until the next leaderboard
    refresh.
  - **The side test** is the registered one. A stamped cell is after the change
    if the carrying merge is an ancestor of, or equal to, its
    `process_version.pipeline_sha`. A cell with no `pipeline_sha` is counted on
    neither side, and its number is listed. Because the boundary is gradual, an
    after-side cell reads the new selection only once a post-promotion fetch (a
    live re-poll or a `document-backfill` apply) has stored the newly selected
    rows for its docket, so the after-side `n` is an upper bound on exposure.

  **How a stored date moves.** `merits_brief_filed` is a fill-in column that
  a fresh non-null parse overwrites, and the live poll re-derives it on every
  poll; the events upsert takes the incoming `opened_at` on an open event. So
  on an affected docket, a post-change poll that finds no adverse brief yet
  derives nothing and the stored date stays; the first poll after the adverse
  brief is filed moves both the column and the open briefed event's
  `opened_at` (and so the committed `event.yaml`) to that filing's date.
  `backfill-response-signals` never revisits a row that already carries a
  date.
  - **Only later, or not at all.** The change can move a date only later or
    leave it unset, never earlier, and never past the real adverse brief,
    which precedes the judgment.
  - **A stale date does not correct itself where no adverse brief comes.** On a
    docket whose judgment is defended only by a Court-appointed amicus (amicus
    filings are excluded from the respondent arm), or whose only respondent
    filed in partial support, no later poll derives a date. The stored date
    stays, and it keeps feeding `merits_event_migration`, which mints the
    briefed moment from the stored column, and the `document-backfill` merits
    gate. Correcting such rows is a corpus mutation, so it would be a pass on
    `run-repair`, decided separately. It is not owed by this entry.
  - **The briefed-moment population changes.** A new docket of that shape now
    opens no respondent-dated briefed moment at all. No membership rule moves,
    but which dockets carry the moment does.

  **What a post-change cell reads.** On an affected docket:
  - a briefed moment that opens at the adverse respondent's brief rather than
    an aligned respondent's;
  - a `merits-brief-respondent` (or reply) document that is the adverse
    party's filing once one is filed and fetched.

  Until then, a row the old selector already stored is still provisioned under
  its kind, because the documents store is latest-wins on `(case, kind)` and
  nothing deletes a row the selector stops selecting. Where no adverse filing
  ever comes, it is provisioned indefinitely. Purging such rows would also be a
  `run-repair` pass, a separate decision this entry does not take. No skill
  movement is predicted, and a movement in **either** direction across this
  boundary may not be read as a model effect.

  `evt-brief-judgment` holds three counted cells from run
  `20261004T201824Z`:

- **A panel figure's rubric signatures are the maximal one-digest-per-judge
  pair sets its points form, 2026-10-12.** A **reading-rule** entry that
  settles how the 2026-10-11 implementation-choices entry's *rubric
  signature* is read, before any `proc-v9` grading exists. It moves no digest,
  no constant, no window and no membership: `uv run fedcourts process-digest
  --all` prints the same `proc-v9` digests, and `COUNTING_WINDOWS` is
  unchanged. It governs the leaderboard's `by_signature` readings on `big_case`
  and `evaluator_agreement`, and any panel figure that later gains a
  per-signature reading.

  **The rule.**

  - **Which signatures are read.** A point's pairs are the (evaluator, digest)
    pairs of every read behind it: for `big_case`, every panel read across the
    case's moments; for a leave-one-out point, the judge's reads and its
    peers' on the case. Of the pair sets that hold one digest per evaluator,
    the signatures read are the **maximal** ones, those no other point's set
    strictly contains. They are derived from the data, not declared.
  - **Membership is by subset.** A point joins the reading of every signature
    that contains all of its pairs. A case only part of a panel read stays
    with the panel it was read under. A point read only under digests two
    signatures share sits in both readings, so readings sharing points are not
    independent and are never differenced as if they were.
  - **A mixed point joins no reading.** A point holding one evaluator under
    two digests sits in no signature's reading. It is counted as
    `mixed_signature_points` and stays in the pooled value, which is coverage.
  - **The minimum clause is read as implied.** The earlier entry requires a
    point to meet the pooled figure's own minimum within a signature. Under
    subset membership every read of a member point carries one of the
    signature's pairs, so a member meets it exactly as it meets the pooled
    one. A point is never re-formed from only its in-signature reads to make
    it a member.
  - **Names.** A reading is named by the union, over its signature's
    digests, of every evaluate label that blessed each digest, from
    `process_version.EVALUATE_BLESSING_LABELS`, never by the labels on the
    stamps. That map is append-only and keeps each digest's labels in blessing
    order: a label that newly blesses a judge digest adds it, and a label that
    carries one forward byte-identical appends itself to that digest's labels,
    so no published reading is ever renamed. The label never partitions
    anything.

  **The alternative not chosen.** A data-independent definition would take
  each label's blessed evaluator digests from the registry as the signatures:
  the `proc-v8` trio and the `proc-v9` trio. It is not chosen because a panel
  need not match a label's set. An evaluator-only re-bless, or a label that
  re-blesses some judges and carries the others forward, puts reads under
  digests from two labels into one point. A label-set rule would then leave
  that point in no reading, or read it by label, which the rule forbids. Under
  either definition, a panel blessed by one label gets one reading.

  **What the choice was made after seeing.** The implementation first grouped
  points by their exact pair set. Over the `proc-v8` resolved slice on
  `staging` that split each predictor's single `proc-v8` panel into fragments
  by which judges happened to give a big-case read, 14, 2, 2 and 87 points for
  `claude-baseline`, every fragment under the same three digests. The output
  that showed the fragmentation also printed each fragment's tau-b (0.809, 1,
  1 and 0.863 for `claude-baseline`), so those values were seen. The choice
  rests on the structure, fragments differing in panel membership and not in
  rubric, and not on the values. On that slice every maximal-signature reading
  equals its pooled value: one reading per figure, the same tau-b over the same
  cases. So the choice moves no published figure.

  **What the date proves.** At `origin/main` `dff75f659`
  (`2026-10-12T15:53:56Z`), four committed predictions carry
  `claude-baseline`'s `proc-v9` digest (`605201bd…`):
  - `scotus/9026000071` `evt-petition-disposition`, run `20261011T142504Z`;
  - `scotus/9026000087` `evt-petition-disposition`, run `20261012T143556Z`;
  - `scotus/73275187` `evt-brief-judgment`, run `20261012T143556Z`;
  - `scotus/73280343` `evt-brief-judgment`, run `20261012T143556Z`.

  No committed evaluation carries any of the three `proc-v9` evaluator digests
  (`167b7d71…`, `18a76b93…`, `22558044…`), and none is stamped `proc-v9`.
  `git grep` over `data/` prints nothing for either. So no panel point under a
  `proc-v9` rubric existed, and no reading this rule governs had an outcome
  under the new rubrics.

- **The cert back-test's Gemini runner retries a zero-exit transient fault;
  recorded 2026-10-12.** A **back-test harness** entry, in the shape of the
  cells' own in-place retry, which the `proc-v9` entry lists among the
  harness changes under unchanged digests. gemini-cli ends a turn whose stream
  went bad (`INVALID_STREAM`) with a zero exit and the fault inside its JSON
  result. Before this change the back-test's Gemini lane read only a non-zero
  exit (its executor did not keep stdout), so such a turn was neither retried
  nor classified: the cell surfaced as a `missing` loss, its fault unnamed.
  From the carrying commit the lane keeps each turn's stdout, and the runner
  classifies every attempt on its result object as well, retries a transient
  one under the runner's own backoff and three-attempt cap from an output root
  reset to its pre-attempt state, and records a zero-exit turn that produced
  nothing as an `engine-failed` loss, or as a spent quota that finishes the
  engine for the campaign. The change also runs the other way, on Gemini's
  non-zero exits: before it, a transient non-zero exit was retried in place
  with no reset whatever the turn had written, as claude's and codex's still
  are; after it, a Gemini turn that already wrote its `prediction.json` or
  `flags.json` is not retried, so a cell that wrote a judgment and then exited
  non-zero on a transient fault, retryable and possibly scored before, is an
  `engine-failed` loss after. No process digest moves, no forward cell runs
  through this runner (the local cascade aside), and no replay cell's
  information set changes; claude and codex are untouched.

  **The reading rule.** A Gemini row in a cert back-test report on either side
  of the carrying commit covers a different share of its campaign's cells
  wherever the engine hit a transient fault: a zero-exit cell lost before may
  be scored after, by a second or third turn, and a non-zero-exit cell that
  had written its judgment may be lost after where a retry scored it before.
  A coverage or loss-rate comparison across the boundary says so, and a
  reason-by-reason comparison of Gemini's `lost_cells` across it reads
  `missing` and `engine-failed` together; a score over the cells both reports
  scored, drawn under the same rule, is unaffected. The committed
  `metrics/cert-backtest.json` records no lost cell for any engine
  (`events_scored` 10 each), so no published figure moves.

  Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-13` (merge commit
  `43933a6382d731bb6f96b269e60cb6f6afeee7a5`, merged `2026-10-13T17:54:17Z`).

- **A prompted fetch's retrieval-log row carries its URL ahead of the
  prompt, 2026-10-12.** A **capture** change of the masking-surface class: no
  digest, no constant, no window and no membership moves, and `uv run
  fedcourts process-digest --all` prints the same `proc-v9` digests. Any call
  whose arguments carry both a `url` and a `prompt`, and no key ranked ahead
  of `prompt` in capture's key order (`q`, `query`, `search`, `citation`),
  keeps both in its 500-character query slice: the URL first and the prompt
  after a newline, so a long prompt loses its tail and never the target. The
  rule keys on the arguments, not the tool name; claude's `WebFetch` is the
  call that has that shape. Every other call keeps the first query key capture
  finds. The slice passes `mask_retrieval_log` unrespelled, so this changes
  what every evaluator reads on the leakage grading's required reading path —
  the URL a fetch reached for, beside the prompt it already saw — under
  unchanged evaluator digests, and it changes what the self-provisioning
  record and any other URL-keyed read of the log can match.

  **What it costs.** The URL takes its length plus one character of the cap
  from the prompt. On `staging` at `ed97094b2` the committed predict logs hold
  415 `WebFetch` rows in 111 claude cells. At a filing URL of about 100
  characters, 76 of them (about 1 in 6) would lose prompt tail, 5,512
  characters in all; at 60 characters, 60 rows and 2,826 characters. The
  median row's slice is 282 characters, and 37 rows already reach the cap.

  **What it reaches.** No number is computed from the slice, but the
  `leakage_suspected` bit graders form from the staged log gates which cells
  every rank key and scored aggregate counts, and the leaderboard publishes the
  result as `leakage_exclusion` (2 of 987 assessed, both gemini-baseline, on
  the committed board). A claude cell captured after the carrying merge
  exposes its fetch targets to that bit and one captured before does not, so
  `leakage_exclusion`'s claude count, and any per-engine comparison of it,
  spans two capture regimes in the middle of the `proc-v9` window under
  unchanged evaluator digests. The change is engine-asymmetric: codex's shell
  fetches and gemini's prompt-embedded fetches were already legible, and only
  claude's prompted fetch moves. Forward cells, where the bit rarely fires,
  are the scored population, which bounds the reach.

  **Why no label bump and no harness-boundary row.** A row minted under the
  rule begins with the URL and a newline, and a row minted before it holds the
  prompt alone; an older prompt that itself opens with a URL reads the same,
  so a row's look is a strong hint and the exact test is `pipeline_sha`
  ancestry against the carrying merge. No predict cell reads anything
  different — capture runs after the engine, on its own log — so it is not a
  `process_version.HARNESS_BOUNDARIES` change, which registers changes to what
  a predict cell reads.

  **What stays blind.** Rows captured before the carrying merge are
  fetch-target-blind on this channel and stay so: their rollouts are gone, so
  no re-capture can restore the URL. Of the 415 committed `WebFetch` rows, 1
  carries `supremecourt.gov` in its slice. The 19 gemini `web_fetch` rows are
  unchanged, since that tool takes its URLs inside the prompt. A
  self-provisioning count, and any URL-keyed audit, over cells minted before
  the carrying merge is a floor on claude's fetch channel in particular, and a
  comparison across that boundary compares two capture regimes.

  **Carrying merge.** promotion/2026-10-13, merge 43933a6382d731bb6f96b269e60cb6f6afeee7a5 at
  2026-10-13T17:54:17Z.

  **Effect check.** On `main`, once a run-predict round after the carrying
  merge has landed a claude cell that used `WebFetch`, `jq -r '.calls[] |
  select(.tool=="WebFetch") | .query | split("\n")[0]'` over that cell's
  `retrieval_log.json` prints URLs, one per fetch.

- **The cert back-test's Gemini cells are admitted their own case tree, not
  their lane's work root; recorded 2026-10-12.** A **back-test harness**
  entry. gemini-cli's file tools are bounded to the launch directory, so an
  off-ledger cell's output root is passed to the CLI as an extra workspace
  directory, and admission also makes that directory a `GEMINI.md`
  context-file discovery root (read at startup, and again whenever a file
  tool touches a path under it). Before this change the whole lane root,
  `<work_dir>/gemini/`, was admitted, so a context file one gemini cell left
  anywhere in the lane would have been read as instructions by every gemini
  cell after it. From the carrying commit the runner admits only the cell's
  own case tree, `<root>/cases/<court>/<docket>/`, which holds everything the
  back-test provisions for the cell and everything its kickoff names. Gemini
  cells for other events of the same case still share that tree, and the
  checkout stays a discovery root for every gemini cell, as before. No
  process digest moves (the admission is runner argv, which no digest
  folds), no forward cell runs through it (a ledger cell is admitted
  nothing, and its command line is unchanged), and claude and codex are
  untouched.

  **The reading rule.** A gemini cell's information set narrows only in
  which context files can reach it. A cell that reached for a provisioned
  input through its file tools reads the same files, and one that reached
  outside its case tree through them falls back to the shell, as an
  off-workspace path always has. A cert back-test before and after the
  carrying commit is compared as before. No published figure moves. In
  today's cert back-test each case tree holds exactly one gemini cell (one
  event per case, one gemini predictor), so the shared-tree residual is
  currently empty; a transient retry of the same cell reuses its tree, so the
  only context file it could meet there is its own.

  The runnable effect check once it is live: on `main`, `uv run pytest
  tests/test_runner.py -k "admits_its_own_case_tree or
  admission_holds_no_other_case"` passes (the runner does not log its argv,
  so the tests are where the admitted path is read); and the next
  `run-backtest` with the gemini lane lands its gemini cells with no file-tool
  refusal for a path outside the workspace in the engine log.

  Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-13` (merge commit

- **The scored boards count each figure's cells by whether their logs show a
  fetch of a court filing, and read a paired figure over the paired events on
  which no engine's log shows one, 2026-10-12.** A **reading-rule** entry that
  registers the first board use of the self-provisioning record. It moves no
  digest, no constant, no window and no membership: `uv run fedcourts
  process-digest --all` prints the same `proc-v9` digests, and
  `COUNTING_WINDOWS` is unchanged. **No rank key, headline figure or score
  reads it, and no cell leaves a headline or ranked figure because of it**;
  its one exclusion is `common_record`'s own event filter, and the committed
  leaderboard is unchanged apart from the two new fields.

  **The rule.**

  - **A cell's reading.** Each scored cell is read off the
    `retrieval_log.json` in its **scored** run's directory (the run the
    grading resolves to, the join every board uses), recomputed from the calls
    rather than read off the log's baked count, so a log captured before the
    count existed reads by the same predicate. `reached`: at least one
    `self_provisioned_fetches` row. `target_blind`: none legible, but a
    fetch-tool row (`WebFetch`, `web_fetch`) whose query slice names no
    `http(s)://` address, so a filing fetch could be hidden there. `unlogged`:
    no resolvable scored prediction or no readable log. `none`: otherwise. A
    cell whose gradings read differently takes the least vouched-for reading,
    in the order `reached`, `target_blind`, `unlogged`, `none`.
  - **The reading is about filings only.** Other retrieval, which a forward
    cell may do without restriction, is neither counted nor excluded on.
  - **`self_provisioning`**, on each pooled entry over its `forward` stratum's
    cells (the stratum its headline figures read), and on each engine in
    `paired` over its paired cells: the cells by reading. Cells, one per
    (case, event, predictor).
  - **`paired.common_record`**: the paired figure restricted to the paired
    events on which every engine's every paired grading reads `none` — the
    paired events on which no engine's log shows a legible fetch of a court
    filing outside the provisioned set. A reach, a target-blind fetch, an
    unread log or a grading missing from the reading on any engine drops the
    event. Each engine's figure is the paired aggregate over its paired
    gradings on those events. Never ranked; the rank stays on the full paired
    figure.

  **How it is read.** `common_record` is a **selected** subset, and the
  selection is not neutral. A cell reaches past the record where the record is
  short and the case contested, so the selection runs on behaviour that tracks
  the outcome and the forecast's uncertainty: it drops grants and close
  petitions first, and it drops an event for one engine's reach whatever the
  others did. Each engine's common-record figure is read against that subset's
  own `always_deny_accuracy` and `in_sample_grant_rate`, never the full paired
  set's, and is never differenced against the paired figure or ranked.

  **The exclusion is engine-asymmetric.** On a log captured before the
  URL-first slice rule (the 2026-10-12 capture entry above), every claude
  `WebFetch` row kept its prompt alone, so `target_blind` drops every event on
  which claude fetched anything at all, while a codex or gemini cell drops an
  event only on a legible filing fetch. That asymmetry is kept rather than
  relaxed: reading a prompt-only fetch as `none` would admit events whose
  information set nothing vouches for. Claude cells captured before that
  rule's carrying merge keep reading `target_blind`, so the `proc-v9` window
  holds claude cells under both regimes, and `reached` is a floor for claude
  until its target-blind cells are gone.

  **What was seen, and in what order.** The proc-v8 common-record figures
  below were computed while the reading was being designed, from builds of
  this code over the committed ledger; nothing in git records the order of
  those builds and the text of this rule, so no claim is made that the rule
  preceded them. Over the committed `proc-v8` ledger (`staging` at
  `8af758f44`), the cert board's paired set is 97 events with 3 grants:
  `claude-baseline` 4 cells reached and 16 target-blind, `codex-baseline` 15
  reached, `gemini-baseline` none, no cell unlogged. 24 events are excluded,
  9 of them by claude's `target_blind` alone. The 73 common-record events hold
  **1** grant: the selection removed 2 of the paired set's 3, one where both
  claude and codex reached and one where claude's fetch is target-blind. On
  them every engine's accuracy is 0.986, which **equals the always-deny floor**
  of that subset (lift 0), and mean Brier is 0.0118, 0.0129 and 0.0209
  (claude, codex, gemini) over one realized grant.

  **What the date proves, and what it does not.** Under the pooled rule a
  predictor's counted cells stay in every later figure, so the `proc-v8`
  events seen above stay inside every later common-record figure; this entry
  is blind only for events first counted after its carrying merge. At
  `origin/main` `a14b36a1e` (`2026-10-12T21:55:06Z`) no committed evaluation
  carries any of the three `proc-v9` evaluator digests (`167b7d71…`,
  `18a76b93…`, `22558044…`; `git grep` over `data/` prints nothing), so
  nothing had been graded since the `proc-v9` cutover. Four committed
  predictions carry `claude-baseline`'s `proc-v9` digest (`605201bd…`), the
  four the rubric-signature entry above lists. The `codex-baseline` and
  `gemini-baseline` `proc-v9` digests (`70fee158…`, `a9033e56…`) are their
  `proc-v8` digests carried forward, so 256 and 253 committed predictions
  carry them, every one predating the cutover's first grading.

  every OT2024, OT2025 and OT2026 cell. **This completes data under the

  pass lands each stub through the live channel's own ingest seam, so it
  arrives parsed and joins the pool. The provisioned statpack's interim
  section is what interim cells anchor on, and its pooled rate is the baseline
  their harness skill is stamped against, so both move for every interim cell
  provisioned or stamped after the next statpack refresh that follows the
  apply. **This entry registers OT2023 alone**; every earlier Term is still
  its own registration.

- **An event whose docket number the Court re-docketed is voided, and its
  gradings leave every scored surface: `scotus/9026000221`
  `evt-petition-arrival-disposition`, 2026-10-14.** A **de-count for a stated
  defect**, at event grain. It moves no digest, no constant, no window and no
  label: `uv run fedcourts process-digest --all` prints the same `proc-v9`
  digests. It narrows the 2026-10-11 statement that revocation is the only
  de-count: revocation stays the only de-count of a **window's** cells, and a
  **void** is the only de-count of a **single event's**, each on its own dated
  entry stating the defect, under the admissibility rule `docs/process-version.md`
  states in *Voiding an event*. A void is registered in
  `src/fedcourtsai/voided_events.json`, a code-owned file, so every void is
  maintainer-merged.

  **The defect, and the ground.** The event's committed outcome records a
  different petition than the one the event was opened on — the rule's one
  ground, `redocketed`. On 2026-08-20 the live channel onboarded the Court's
  No. 26-221 as *Mara Nathan et al. v. Alamo Heights Independent School
  District* (Fifth Circuit No. 25-50695, docketed August 20, 2026), opened
  this arrival event under that caption, and predict run `20260820T231432Z`
  forecast it: claude-baseline 0.72, codex-baseline 0.72, gemini-baseline
  0.90, each a forecast of Nathan. The Court then re-docketed: No. 26-221
  became *Theodore James Purdy v. Kansas* (Court of Appeals of Kansas No.
  126,981, docketed August 21, 2026), and Nathan appears to sit at No. 26-257.
  The event's `outcome.json` records Purdy's denial on 2026-10-13, and
  evaluate run `20261014T154957Z` graded the three Nathan forecasts against it.

  **Shown outcome-blind, from stored payloads alone.** The content store's
  dated snapshots of `scotus/9026000221` are the Court's own docket JSON for
  `CaseNumber 26-221`: the 2026-08-20 snapshot names Nathan, the Fifth Circuit
  number and a docketed date of August 20; every snapshot from 2026-10-05 on
  names Purdy, the Kansas number and a docketed date of August 21. The case has
  no snapshot between those dates, so the re-docketing fell between polls. The
  ingest recorded what the Court served; what failed is that nothing compares
  a stored docket's identity across snapshots.

  **How it was detected: outcome-triggered.** codex-judge flagged a blocker
  and claude-judge a warning on the graded event, and the agent-feedback
  triage of 2026-10-14 surfaced them. The defect was then confirmed from the
  payloads above, without reference to the outcome's value or the scores. No
  systematic scan has been run, so **the voids so far may be incomplete**:
  unchecked pending detection are the single-event graded live cases
  `scotus/9026000006`, `9026000027`, `9026000045`, `9026000139`,
  `9026000152` and `9026000173`, and the 168 SCOTUS cases on `main` at
  `5643cbbee` holding a committed prediction on an event not yet resolved.

  **What is removed, and what it scored.** The six gradings of the three
  forecasts: claude-judge and codex-judge, each over claude-baseline,
  codex-baseline and gemini-baseline, all under the `proc-v9` judge digests
  (`167b7d71…`, `18a76b93…`). **All six were misses** (`correct: 0`), with
  Brier 0.5184 (claude-baseline), 0.5184 (codex-baseline) and 0.81
  (gemini-baseline) under each judge. gemini-judge has no grading on the
  event. `store.stratify` drops the gradings after the run collapse and before
  any stratum, window composition, forward-claim or leakage denominator counts
  them; the agreement views and the tool-usefulness join drop the event's
  reads; no evaluate cell is minted for it on any route, so gemini-judge's
  missing grading is never owed; the big-case board shows its outcome as none;
  and the export carries the three predictions with `voided` true and null
  outcome columns. Every reader asks the one predicate in
  `src/fedcourtsai/voids.py`, which is code-owned with the registry. No
  committed file is edited: the predictions, the gradings and the outcome stay
  in `data/` as written.

  **Why the sibling event is not voided.** The same case's
  `evt-petition-disposition` was opened on 2026-08-21 under Purdy's caption,
  predicted in run `20261005T153213Z` from Purdy's 2026-10-05 snapshot, its
  documents name neither Nathan nor Alamo Heights, and its outcome is Purdy's
  own denial: event and outcome describe one petition.

  **Why a void, and not a revocation or a corrected outcome.** A window's
  revocation de-counts a whole protocol, and these cells' window is not
  defective. A corrected outcome (`stamp-cell --regrade`) re-scores an event
  against its true outcome, which this event has none of at this docket
  number. The better remedy would re-resolve the event against Nathan's own
  outcome; nothing relocates an event between dockets today, so this entry
  instead commits to recording Nathan's eventual disposition under No. 26-257
  beside this void once it lands.

- **Counting instants and bless moments are stamped by the carrying merge, 2026-10-14.**
  A **procedure** entry that declares how every label registered from now on
  gets its instants. It moves no digest, no constant, no window and no
  membership: `uv run fedcourts process-digest --all` prints the same
  `proc-v9` digests, and the committed registry holds no pending row. The rows
  already registered keep the instants they hold, `proc-v9`'s hand-set
  `2026-10-11T12:00:00Z` counting instant included.

  **The rule.** From the next label on, a label is registered in the PR that
  moves the digests (`fedcourts register-process`), as **pending** rows, and
  the promotion merge that carries that PR to `main` stamps them:
  - the label's counting instant, the bless moment of every digest it newly
    blesses, the opening of every window it opens (and the close of every
    window it closes), and the instant of every harness boundary it registers
    are all **that merge's git committer time**, written by
    the `promotion-record` writer with `source: "merge"`;
  - **no instant is forecast by hand.** The shakedown margin a hand-set late
    counting instant used to buy — a span after the merge in which honest
    cells landed uncounted — is dropped. It bought nothing the stamp does not
    give: the bytes are immutable from the merge, nothing can carry the new
    digest before the merge lands it, and the gate's Step 0 refuses a batch
    whose pending digest already stamps a committed cell. What it cost was a
    span of honest cells re-owed and paid for twice. The closing side keeps a
    straddle of its own: a cell of the superseded digest in flight at the
    carrying merge and stamped after it falls after its window's close, so it
    is shakedown, uncounted and re-owed, exactly as a hand-margin cell was on
    the opening side. The promotion gate's quiescence check (docs/pipeline.md,
    *Promotion*) keeps that set empty in practice, and any residue shows in
    `fedcourts successor-disclosures` as cells carrying the closed digest
    stamped at or after the close;
  - **an evaluator-only label holds the prior counting instant**, opens and
    closes no window, and only its new evaluator blessings are stamped — the
    evaluator-half supersession rule in `docs/process-version.md`;
  - **one label per digest-moving promotion.** Step 0 refuses a batch carrying
    more than one label new to `main`, so each label has one carrying merge,
    one instant and one `prereg/` tag;
  - **`prereg/<label>` sits on the carrying merge**, an annotated tag the
    writer creates with the plan's message, not on a freeze commit: the merge
    is what fixes the instant, so it is the commit the label is audited
    against. This departs from the freeze-commit convention the earlier
    `prereg/` tags follow;
  - **"merged" times in fills are git committer time**
    (`git log -1 --format=%cI <merge>`), the one clock git re-derives.
    `promotion/2026-10-13`'s fills recorded `2026-10-13T17:54:17Z`, GitHub's
    `mergedAt`; its committer time is `17:54:16Z`. The second touches no cell:
    that merge stamped no registry row, and no prediction or evaluation on
    `main` is stamped inside it.

  **Fills.** The writer fills only placeholders the merge itself added, from a
  closed key set: the promotion tag, the merge hash and the merged time, and a
  keyed census of committed artifacts carrying given digest prefixes, rendered
  by `fedcourts digest-census` over the merge's own tree. A census counts
  **carrying files** — every stamped cell, shakedown and de-counted ones
  included — never counted cells, and an entry's wording says "carrying".
  Free-text placeholders stay a maintainer's, and the writer lists them on the
  promotion PR.

  **Pending rows read conservatively** until the merge stamps them: a pending
  blessing is registered but has no bless moment, so a board counts no
  prediction under it; a cell stamped with a pending digest is pending, not
  de-counted, so the backlog re-owes nothing; a pending label leaves the prior
  counting instant in force; a window whose opening is pending counts nothing
  and one whose close is pending stays open; a pending harness boundary splits
  nothing. A board built meanwhile names what it read as pending.

  **Step 0 is the promotion gate's**, on every batch (`scripts/promotion-gate.sh
  registry`): it refuses a pending registration on a `main` that does not yet
  hold this declaration, a pending digest that already stamps a committed cell
  on `main`, an enabled actor whose digest is unregistered, a predictor with
  more than one open window, more than one new label or one whose `prereg/` tag
  exists, a repeated boundary name, and a pending row already sitting on
  `main`.

  **When it takes effect.** The registry's `merge_stamping_declared` names this
  entry's date, and the writer stamps only where the merge's **first parent**
  — what `main` held before the merge — holds both that field and this
  heading. So the promotion carrying this entry cannot itself stamp anything:
  the first label stamped under the rule rides a later promotion.

  Census at `origin/main` `4e505acc0` (2026-10-14T23:03:49Z), counting
  carrying files: 25 predictions carrying `proc-v9`'s claude-baseline digest
  (`605201bd`); 277 carrying codex-baseline's digest carried from `proc-v8`

  evaluations carrying a `proc-v9` judge digest (`167b7d71`, `18a76b93`,

  predictions carrying a digest carried from `proc-v8`:

- **Engine CLI updates under an unchanged process digest are composition, and
  each cell records the engine version that ran, 2026-10-14.** A
  **reading-rule** entry with a harness change beside it. It moves no digest,
  no constant, no window and no membership: `uv run fedcourts process-digest
  --all` prints the same six `proc-v9` digests.

  **What changes.** The three engine CLIs every cell, smoke and labeler runs
  are pinned once each, in `.github/engines/<engine>/` (an exact version
  and its lockfile), and every workflow installs from that pin through one
  action. The claude cells hand `claude-code-action` the pinned binary
  instead of the CLI the action bundles, and `codex-action` takes its version
  from the same pin. Dependabot proposes each engine release as its own PR
  about three days after it ships, each validated by both integration engine
  smokes before it merges.

  **The reading rule.** An engine CLI update under an unchanged process digest
  is **composition**, not a series break: the predictor's record keeps
  accruing across it, as it does across a harness boundary. A by-engine-version
  cut is available to any reading that wants to ask whether an update moved
  anything, and it is a comparison over different events, flagged as such. A
  **model** change remains a digest move and a new label; nothing here changes
  that.

  **The record.** Every cell's harness-written `usage.json` carries
  `engine_version`: the version the engine's own binary reports, read by the
  harness, never the agent's word. For claude-code and gemini, which the
  harness installs, the read is taken at install, before any agent runs;
  codex is installed by its action, so its read follows the run. A post-run
  read that disagrees with the install-time one, or a read other than the
  pinned version, is kept in the same file as `engine_version_discrepancy`,
  and a cut by engine version treats that cell as unknown. Cells written before
  this entry's carrying merge do not carry it. For them the engine version is
  recoverable only from the run's job log, which expires, and a cut by engine
  version treats them as unknown rather than guessing.

  **Pinning moves nothing today.** The versions pinned are the ones cells
  already ran:
  - **Claude Code 2.1.289.** The claude predict cell of run 38441480911
    (2026-10-13) logged `claude-agent-sdk@0.3.289` and then `Installing Claude
    Code v2.1.289 … Version: 2.1.289`: the CLI the action bundled at the
    pinned `claude-code-action` v1.0.241. The smokes and the labeler had
    pinned 2.1.280, so they move up to what the cells run, and a smoke now
    tests the version production uses.
  - **Codex 0.144.1** and **Gemini CLI 0.49.0.** The cells already pinned
    these literally (`codex-version`, and the Gemini install step).

  Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-15` (merge commit
  `1850188d9e7ff698d3146f55e27e5a5ac7cb7c5c`, merged `2026-10-15T19:14:30Z`).

  The runnable effect check once it is live: the first predict round after the
  carrying merge writes `usage.json` files whose `engine_version` reads
  `2.1.289`, `0.144.1` or `0.49.0` by engine, for example `jq -r
  '.engine + " " + (.engine_version // "none")'` over that round's
  `usage.json` files; and a claude cell's job log shows the action using the
  supplied executable rather than installing its own.

- **A forward predict cell is refused when a pre-mint poll finds its event
  already decided, and each cell records a docket poll before and after it
  ran, 2026-10-15.** A **provisioning** change that alters which forward cells
  mint. It moves no digest, no constant and no window: `uv run fedcourts
  process-digest --all` prints the same `proc-v9` digests, and what a minted
  cell reads is unchanged. It does change membership, by a rule correlated
  with the outcome; see *What the refusal selects*.

  **The defect it closes.** A forward cell is provisioned from the corpus's
  latest stored snapshot, which can be days behind the docket, and a
  disposition's `resolved_at` is a date with no time of day. A cell minted
  from a snapshot that predates the day's order could therefore run after the
  order was public, and nothing in the record could say which came first.
  Counted on `origin/main` at `893ba48d3` (2026-10-15T17:54:24Z), with each
  cell's clock read from the harness's `stamped_at` (UTC) and dated in Court
  local time (America/New_York), the clock `resolved_at` is dated in: 26 of
  the 108 resolved forward interim predictions were written on or after their
  outcome's decision date. 23 were written on the day itself —
  `scotus/9526000428` ×6, 9526000434 ×3, 9526000437 ×3, 9526000447 ×2
  (`proc-v8`, 14 cells) and 9526000477 ×9 (`proc-v9`) — and 3 after it, all on
  9526000256 (two `proc-v4`, one `proc-v5`, labels before `proc-v8`, whose
  cells are de-counted). By engine the 26 split claude 9, codex 9, gemini 8.
  None of the 394 resolved forward cert predictions was written on or after its
  decision date. Dated in UTC instead, four `scotus/9526000275` cells stamped
  01:13Z–01:17Z on 2026-09-03 would also count; that is the evening of
  2026-09-02 in Court time, before the 2026-09-03 denial, so they are a
  UTC-only artefact and are not counted here. All 9 resolved `proc-v9` forward
  interim cells are exposed (26A477), so any `proc-v9` forward interim figure
  today rests entirely on decision-day cells. On 2026-10-14 the forward cells
  for 9526000477 (26A477) were stamped between 15:54:01Z and 18:27:02Z, the day
  the order denying the application as moot issued, from a 2026-10-08
  snapshot; in evaluate run `20261015T154823Z` both judges could only flag the
  ordering as unresolvable.

  **The rule.** From this entry's carrying merge, `run-predict` provisions every
  forward cell with `provision-snapshot --pre-mint-poll`. Just before the
  record is written, the harness fetches the docket's current JSON from the
  Court and runs the same outcome scan the forward gate runs on the stored
  snapshot (`pipeline.outcome.forward_leakage`). The fetch is bounded: a 10 s
  per-phase timeout, at most one retry, and an 18 s total deadline checked
  before every request and redirect hop, so a poll is up to two GETs. The
  deadline does not bound a body trickling in under the per-phase timeout. A
  decided event refuses the cell (exit 3) and nothing is minted. An open one is
  recorded in the cell's `usage.json` as `pre_mint_poll`: `polled_at` (when the
  fetch began, UTC), the docket number, the state and a reason. A poll that
  cannot answer — not a SCOTUS docket, no live spelling, no docket served, a
  body that is not JSON, a timeout, the spent deadline, any error in the fetch
  or the scan — records `unavailable`, and the cell proceeds on the
  stored-snapshot gates, as every cell did before this entry. The poll applies
  to every forward cell, cert and interim alike: an order list issues a day's
  cert dispositions at once, which is the same exposure. After the engine
  stops, a second step polls the same docket number once more and records the
  result as `post_run_poll`. That poll only records; it never refuses or
  removes a cell. A cell's two polls make up to four GETs.

  **What `open` means.** At `polled_at` the Court's docket JSON, as served,
  carried no disposition the scan recognises. It is not proof the event was
  undecided: the JSON can lag the order or be served from a cache, the scan's
  recall is not perfect, and a disposition can land after the poll. A
  `pre_mint_poll` and a `post_run_poll` both reading `open` say the run ended
  before the served docket showed a decision — not that the order was
  unpublished, since an order list or a press account can precede the docket
  JSON. With an open pre-mint poll and a later `decided` or absent post-run
  poll, the cell's exposure window is `[polled_at, cell end]`, and within it
  the ordering of order and run stays unresolvable from the polls. Whether a
  cell actually saw the outcome is judged from its retrieval log's content in
  every case, not from the polls.

  **What the refusal selects.** Refusal is a membership rule, and the rule is
  correlated with the outcome. A disposition that issues quickly, before the
  next round mints, is refused; one that lingers is predicted. Among the 18
  applications (37 events) with resolved forward interim predictions on
  `origin/main` at `893ba48d3`, the 6 with a cell written on or after the
  decision date (5 of them on the day itself) split 5 denied / 1 granted,
  against 12 / 5 / 1 (denied / granted / withdrawn) overall and 7 / 4 / 1
  among the 12 that were not exposed. The refused set is plausibly
  denial-weighted; the size of that selection is unmeasured, and the counts are
  too small to estimate it. The same rule thins forward cert cells, though none
  was exposed in the ledger above. The refusal is recorded durably: the cell's
  `status.json` carries `pre_mint_refusal` (`polled_at`, reason), and the
  collect job rolls every refused cell into a per-engine section of the run PR
  body and of the agent-feedback issue comment — posted even when the round has
  nothing else to report — and does not count it as a cell that produced
  nothing, against the attempt cap or as a dead engine.

  **Engines.** The poll runs in each engine's cell independently, so a
  disposition landing between two engines' provisioning steps can refuse one
  and mint the other. A paired comparison over events every engine produced
  absorbs that; a pooled per-engine figure does not, so any per-engine figure
  is read beside that engine's refusal count, which is why the roll-up is keyed
  per engine.

  **Re-owing.** A refused cell leaves no output, so a later round's planner
  owes it again while the corpus still shows the event pending, and each such
  round refuses it again. The roll-up therefore repeats a refusal across
  rounds: de-duplicate it by (event, engine) before reading it as cells
  removed. If a later round's poll is `unavailable`, the cell mints on the
  stored-snapshot gates as before; the earlier roll-up is what shows it was
  once refused. For an interim cell, the refusal plausibly leaves its
  salience-reserve slot held until a corpus pull records the disposition,
  since the reserve reads the same stored state that still shows the
  application pending; this is unverified.

  **What it does not do.** It does not prevent a disposition that lands after
  the poll on the same day. It does not change what a cell reads: the fresh
  payloads are evidence for the gate and the record only, never staged, and the
  cell still reads the stored snapshot. It de-counts nothing already committed:
  the 26 cells above stay as they are, flagged by the judges where they were
  graded. No scored figure sets them aside; whether one should is a scoring
  decision this entry does not make.

  **Reading the polls.** Guidance for a reader, which no figure applies yet: a
  pre-mint poll reading `open` is taken as establishing that the cell began
  against a docket that did not yet show the outcome, within the residuals
  above. A poll reading `unavailable`, or a missing poll, is unknown —
  whatever the cell's date, because the usage capture is best-effort and a
  missing field does not prove a cell predates the carrying merge.

  **The record.** `pre_mint_poll` and `post_run_poll` sit on the
  harness-written `usage.json`, so they are never the agent's word. Each
  reaches the usage step as a step output, fixed outside any file the agent can
  reach; the post-run poll takes its docket number from the pre-mint poll's
  output, never from the cell's record. A `decided` pre-mint poll never
  reaches `usage.json`, because a refused cell writes none; a `decided`
  post-run poll does, since that poll only records. Cells written before the
  carrying merge carry no poll, and their ordering on a decision day stays
  unresolvable.

  Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-15` (merge commit
  `1850188d9e7ff698d3146f55e27e5a5ac7cb7c5c`, merged `2026-10-15T19:14:30Z`).

  The runnable effect check once it is live: the first predict round after the
  carrying merge writes forward-cell `usage.json` files with both polls, for
  example `jq -r '[.pre_mint_poll.state, .post_run_poll.state] | map(. //
  "none") | join(" ")'` over that round's `usage.json` files prints `open open`
  (or `unavailable` in either place). A cell whose docket was already decided
  at mint shows `refusing to provision forward cell … the live docket polled at
  …` in its job log, no committed output, and a row under *Pre-mint refusals*
  in the round's run PR body or agent-feedback comment.

- **A Court docket that withholds the petitioner's counsel block is read as
  self-represented on the petitioner side by both contact scrubs,
  2026-10-15.** A **conditioning** entry in the *what the pipeline provisions*
  class. The docket-level trigger (`unrepresented_sides`) reads an absent side
  as **unknown**, which the 2026-09-21 entry registered so that the
  CourtListener REST shape, which carries no counsel blocks anywhere, is not
  scrubbed because of its payload shape. The Court serves a pseudonymous
  self-represented petitioner's docket the same way it serves any other
  docket, except that the `Petitioner` key is missing. That petitioner's
  staged petition therefore stayed unscrubbed. This was observed in evaluate
  run `20261005T221055Z` on `scotus/73372297` (No. 25-1300). Its provisioned
  `petition.txt` carried two email-pattern matches with
  `contact_scrubbed: false`, and claude-judge flagged it. The committed
  ledger for that case holds no email match. The staged text is runner-local
  and never committed, so nothing was published.

  No prompt byte and no registry field moves, so no digest moves:
  `uv run fedcourts process-digest --all` at this commit prints `proc-v9` and
  the six digests `605201bd…` (claude-baseline), `70fee158…`
  (codex-baseline), `a9033e56…` (gemini-baseline), `167b7d71…`
  (claude-judge), `18a76b93…` (codex-judge) and `22558044…` (gemini-judge).

  **What changes.** One absence is now read as evidence
  (`withholds_petitioner_block`). A payload qualifies when all three of
  these hold:
  - it is the Court's own docket shape, meaning it carries
    `ProceedingsandOrder`, which a CourtListener REST docket never does;
  - it carries the respondent side's counsel key, meaning the `Respondent`
    key or its `AttorneyHeaderRespondent` heading;
  - it carries **no** `Petitioner` key.

  All three are tests of **key presence**, never of a key's value. A payload
  carrying `ProceedingsandOrder` and an empty `Respondent` list therefore
  qualifies. The error this admits is an over-scrub, which withholds counsel's
  professional details and never stages a filer's own.

  Such a payload reads `Petitioner` in `unrepresented_sides`. Every reader of
  that trigger moves with it:
  - **The staged documents** get the shape pass. No petitioner block is
    served, so there is no value to key the value pass on. The manifest reads
    `contact_scrub_passes` `["shape"]`. Where the payload also qualifies on
    its `Other` list alone, the documents move from `["value"]` to
    `["value", "shape"]`.
  - **The staged snapshot** has no petitioner block to withhold. The
    respondent's counsel block stays as served, and the run log echoes `0
    value(s) withheld on 0 petitioner-side block(s)`.
  - **A consolidated member's borrow** refuses a lead that withholds its
    petitioner block, as it already refuses a lead whose party side reads
    self-represented. The member then stages none of that lead's merits
    filings.

  The following stay as they were:
  - a `Petitioner` key served empty or null, which is still read as nothing;
  - a CourtListener REST docket;
  - a Court docket carrying neither side's counsel key;
  - every docket that serves a petitioner block.

  **A known residual.** The third item above is not closed. A pseudonymous
  self-represented petitioner whose docket the Court serves with no counsel key
  on either side, typically before the respondent appears, still stages its
  text as filed. On that payload nothing tells a withheld block apart from a
  docket the Court has not yet populated. The census below counts these
  dockets, so the residual is sized rather than assumed.

  **The trade.** The shape pass runs over every staged document on such a
  docket, including a brief in opposition filed by the respondent's counsel,
  as it already does on any docket read as self-represented on a party side.
  That counsel's professional contact details are withheld, and legal prose
  the shape pass misreads is withheld with them.

  **The population.** Triage counted **76** SCOTUS rows in blob `c85bda09…`
  (newest pull stamp `2026-10-05`) that carry counsel but no petitioner-role
  block. **14** of them are salience-selected and **4** are pending. That
  figure was read off the corpus row's counsel, not by running this predicate
  over each row's latest payload. The real-predicate read is a read-only
  script in the carrying PR's description, run over the latest live snapshot
  and stored documents of every SCOTUS row. For each class (newly scrubbed,
  value-only to value+shape, or unchanged) it gives the number of dockets,
  how many are selected and how many pending, and the total spans the scrub
  withholds. It also counts the residual above, Court-shaped payloads with
  neither counsel key, split into selected and pending. It prints no value.
  Its summary counts, with the blob's sha and its `corpus-info` vintage, go
  on the next line, which must stay one line of plain prose with no angle
  bracket or backtick:
  At corpus blob 5d4bac58cb9b20bbc2827b08c375914f19cfddf7eb135ae48ac93c7dad3f814e, freshness latest pull 2026-10-17, latest snapshot 2026-07-13, corpus-check run 39041844535 at a0c0ba591: 25805 live-slice SCOTUS rows walked, 25682 with a live snapshot; 113 carry a withheld petitioner block, 112 newly scrubbed (15 selected, 4 pending, 40 with stored documents, 425 spans withheld), 0 value-only to value+shape, 1 unchanged; 54 residual rows carry the Court shape with neither counsel key (0 selected, 2 pending).

  **A harness boundary under the 2026-10-11 pooled rule.** The change moves
  what a predict cell reads under unchanged digests, so it is composition and
  not a cut. The pooled default and the paired figure keep both sides and list
  each engine's `n` before and after. It cuts only a figure that reads its own
  effect.
  - **The registry row.** The boundary is `scrub-withheld-petitioner-block`.
    It applies to every predictor, its reach is `self-represented dockets`,
    and it is not gradual: provisioning reads the payload already stored, so
    the next cell provisioned on an affected docket reads the change, with no
    back-fill needed. The row is registered **pending** in the change's own
    PR (`fedcourts register-boundary`), under the 2026-10-14 merge-stamping
    declaration. Its `merge` and `at` are null until the promotion merge that
    carries it to `main` stamps them with that merge's SHA and committer time
    (`promotion-record`). Until then the row is left out of
    `process_version.HARNESS_BOUNDARIES`, so no cell has a side of it. A board
    built meanwhile names it under `frozen_process.pending`.
  - **The side test** is the registered one. A stamped cell is after the change
    if the carrying merge is an ancestor of, or equal to, its
    `process_version.pipeline_sha`. A cell with no `pipeline_sha` is counted on
    neither side, and its number is listed.
  - **Exposure is an upper bound,** as for the earlier scrub boundaries. Whether
    a docket withholds its petitioner block lives only in the corpus, so the
    after-side `n` counts the cells that could have read the change, not the
    cells that did.

  **What a post-change cell reads.** On an affected docket, the cell reads a
  subset of the pre-change document text and the same snapshot. Its
  `documents.json` reads `contact_scrubbed: true` with `contact_scrub_passes`
  `["shape"]`, where before it read `false` with `[]`. That holds on every
  staged document, including one whose text does not change. On a
  consolidated member whose lead withholds its petitioner block, the borrowed
  merits filings are no longer staged. No skill movement is predicted. A
  movement in **either** direction across this boundary may not be read as a
  model effect.

  **What does not move.** No base rate re-prices, no membership rule moves and
  no scored figure moves. Nothing is written to the corpus. The corpus row,
  the content-store payload and the source PDF are untouched. The three lanes
  that stage through this provisioning narrow the same way from the carrying
  promotion on: predict cells, evaluate cells and the case-summary lane's
  `summary-stage`. Summaries that already exist are not re-derived, and a
  summary's record digest is taken from the corpus payload, so the change
  moves no digest and re-owes no summary. Cells already run on an affected
  docket stay as they are. They read the filer's details as filed, which is
  more information, not leaked information.

  **The amendment debt.** It is unchanged. This entry adds no new token.

  Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-16` (merge commit

  The runnable effect check once it is live:
  - `uv run pytest tests/test_documents.py tests/test_cli_provision.py -k
    withholding_the_petitioner` is green;
  - `uv run fedcourts process-digest --all` still prints `proc-v9` and the
    six digests above;
  - `uv run fedcourts provision-snapshot --court scotus --docket 73372297`
    (with the data root pointed at a scratch directory) echoes `contact
    scrub: N detail(s) withheld across M staged document(s) (no attorney
    named for the petitioner; passes: shape only)` with a non-zero `N`, while
    its latest payload still serves no `Petitioner` key;
  - on `main` once the boundary row is stamped, `uv run python -c "from
    fedcourtsai.process_version import HARNESS_BOUNDARIES as H;
    print('scrub-withheld-petitioner-block' in {b.name for b in H})"` prints
