- **The cert back-test headlines the granted-or-not axis; recorded
  2026-10-21.** A **reading-rule** entry, recorded ahead of the promotion that
  carries the change and of the first scheduled report it governs. It moves
  no digest and no forward figure.

  **Why.** The report ranked and headlined `lift_over_always_denied`, an
  exact-disposition accuracy minus the denied share. A Rule 46 dismissal or a
  withdrawal is not an outcome a cert forecaster is asked to call, so on that
  axis every such petition was a miss for every forecaster and for the floor.
  The 2026-10-03 run's ten petitions held one (25-960, dismissed 2026-07-17).
  Brier already binarised the same petitions to not granted.

  **What moved.** Three fields join the report:
  - `always_not_granted_accuracy` is the set's not-granted share, which is
    always-deny's `granted_accuracy`.
  - `granted_lift_over_always_denied` on each entry is `granted_accuracy`
    minus that share, over the petitions the entry was scored on.
  - `granted_correct` on each arm counts the entry's granted-or-not calls
    there.

  The board ranks by the granted lift, then Brier, then id, with whole-set
  entries above short ones as before. The review PR's top line and per-arm
  table, and the weekly digest's floor and per-arm scores, are stated on that
  axis, and both surfaces name the axis beside the floor. A GVR counts as a
  grant and a dismissal or withdrawal does not, which is the projection
  `granted_flag` already applied to Brier and `granted_accuracy`.

  **What did not move.** The draw, the population and the scope are
  unchanged. No petition is excluded by its outcome. `accuracy`,
  `always_denied_accuracy`, `lift_over_always_denied` and every arm's
  `correct`, `denied` and `lift_over_always_denied` keep their
  exact-disposition meaning as a secondary reading. Brier, calibration and
  the band segments are unchanged. No prompt template, agent config or
  `src/fedcourtsai/process_version.py` moved, and the forward leaderboard's
  exact-match always-deny floor is a different instrument this entry does
  not touch.

  **The reading rule.** A report with `always_not_granted_accuracy` was ranked
  on the granted axis, and one without it was ranked on exact disposition.
  The two lifts are not differenced across that boundary. On a draw with no
  dismissal or withdrawal the two floors are equal, and the two lifts differ
  only where a forecaster's disposition label missed inside the same
  granted-or-not call. The standing report on `main` (run
  `20261017T115347Z`, ten petitions) is such a draw: every entry's
  `accuracy` equals its `granted_accuracy` at 0.9 against a 0.9 floor, so
  its board would rank the same on either axis.

  The runnable effect check once it is live: the first
  `metrics/cert-backtest.json` landed after the carrying promotion has a
  non-null `.always_not_granted_accuracy` equal to one minus the grant-family
  share of its set. Every entry carries `.granted_lift_over_always_denied`,
  and `jq --argjson n "$(jq .events_scored metrics/cert-backtest.json)"
  '[.entries[] | select(.events_scored == $n) | .granted_lift_over_always_denied]
  | . == (sort | reverse)' metrics/cert-backtest.json` prints `true`. The review PR's
  floor line reads "on granted vs not".

- **A respondent's brief confessing error no longer dates the briefed moment,
  and a Court-appointed amicus's brief does; recorded 2026-10-22.** A
  **provisioning-cutoff** change with a harness boundary, recorded ahead of
  the promotion that carries it.

  **Why.** The briefed moment is the point at which both sides' arguments are
  on the record. Before the change, a respondent's brief "in support of
  reversal" or "supporting vacatur" opened it, and that brief argues the
  petitioner's side. The defense of the judgment comes later, from an adverse
  co-respondent or from an amicus the Court appoints to defend it. Observed on
  25-5343 (`scotus/73277583`): its `evt-brief-judgment` opened `2026-06-30`,
  the day the United States filed "supporting vacatur", while the appointed
  amicus's brief was filed `2026-08-25`. The appointed amicus's brief opened
  nothing at all, because the respondent arm excludes every amicus filing, so
  a docket the amicus alone defends had no briefed moment.

  **What moved.** Only `respondent_brief_date`, the briefed moment's date:
  - `is_respondent_merits_brief` refuses an entry "in support of" or
    "supporting" reversal or vacatur.
  - The new `is_appointed_amicus_merits_brief` reads "Brief of Court-appointed
    amicus curiae …" and "Brief amicus curiae of Court-appointed amicus curiae
    …", and `respondent_brief_date` takes the first post-grant entry either
    predicate reads.

  The consolidated member's borrow (`member_respondent_brief_date`, which
  fills `merits_brief_on_lead`) reads the same function. An appointed amicus
  names no party, so the member's side filter keeps its brief for every member
  of the group, unless the Clerk marks it "(as to No.)" for other dockets
  only, which drops it. `merits_brief_on_lead` is fill-in latched, so a member
  date already latched off a confession of error stays. No mint reads that
  column, and its movement was not measured here. What stays: all
  four merits arms of the selector, the member's side filter and the
  `document-backfill` gap floor. A confession of error is still stored and
  provisioned as `merits-brief-respondent`, and its description is the
  entry's text, which says which way it argues.

  No prompt byte and no registry field moves, so no digest moves:
  `uv run fedcourts process-digest --all` at this commit prints `proc-v10` and
  the six digests `605201bd…` (claude-baseline), `7ab92dd4…`
  (codex-baseline), `bee46e92…` (gemini-baseline), `167b7d71…`
  (claude-judge), `a8610eec…` (codex-judge) and `6a88d3dc…` (gemini-judge),
  identical with and without the change.

  **A harness boundary under the 2026-10-11 pooled rule.** The change moves
  when a predict cell's briefed moment opens under unchanged digests. It is
  composition, not a cut, as for `merits-brief-partial-support`: the pooled
  default and the paired figure keep both sides and list each engine's `n`
  before and after. It cuts only a figure that reads its own effect, such as
  a briefed-moment lead time. A cert-stage cell and the merits grant moment
  read no merits brief, so neither is affected.
  - **The registry row.** The boundary is `merits-brief-confession-of-error`:
    `HarnessBoundary("merits-brief-confession-of-error", <carrying promotion
    merge hash>, <its committer time, UTC>, None, "granted dockets",
    gradual=True)`. It applies to every predictor, and it is gradual because
    the moved date reaches a docket only through a later poll. Its carrying
    merge exists only once the promotion merges, so the row joins
    `process_version.HARNESS_BOUNDARIES` in the post-promotion fill PR that
    completes this entry's placeholders, as the earlier rows did.
  - **The side test** is the registered one: a stamped cell is after the
    change if the carrying merge is an ancestor of, or equal to, its
    `process_version.pipeline_sha`.

  **How a stored date moves.** As the `merits-brief-partial-support` entry
  states it: the live poll re-derives `merits_brief_filed` on a pending
  docket, a fresh non-null parse overwrites it, and the events upsert takes
  the new `opened_at` on an open event. So on a pending docket the date moves
  at the first post-change poll. A decided docket is not polled, and
  `backfill-response-fields`, which run-seed sweeps daily, fills only a row
  whose `merits_brief_filed` is null. So the decided dockets split:
  - the eight that move from none to a date are filled by that sweep without
    anyone acting;
  - the ten that move from one date to another keep the old stored date.

  None of them opens a moment, since the mint refuses a row with a latched
  judgment, but a replay cell that reads a decided prior's
  `merits_brief_filed` reads a mixed population: new dates on the eight, old
  ones on the ten. Correcting the ten is a corpus mutation and would be a
  `run-repair` pass, decided separately; this entry does not owe it. Unlike
  the partial-support change, this one can move a date earlier: on 24-362 the
  appointed amicus filed a day before the respondent. An appointed amicus's
  brief dates the moment on any docket where it is the first defending brief,
  not only after a confession of error.

  **What a post-change cell reads.** On an affected docket:
  - after a confession of error, a briefed cell placed after the defending
    brief, so it holds both sides' briefs;
  - on a 24-362-shape docket, a briefed cell placed before the respondent's
    own brief, with the appointed amicus's defense on the record;
  - on 25-5930, a newly owed briefed cell opening at `2026-09-18`.

  No skill movement is predicted, and a movement in **either** direction
  across this boundary may not be read as a model effect.

- **A predict cell stages its `Vide`-linked dockets under `record/related/`;
  recorded 2026-10-22.** A **provisioning-cutoff** change with a harness
  boundary, recorded ahead of the promotion that carries it.

  **Why.** The Court's docket JSON links a cross-petition, a companion case
  or the petition a case is held for as `Vide` in `RelatedCaseNumber`, on both
  dockets. A cell had no record of the linked docket's state. Claude cells
  recovered it by fetching supremecourt.gov and codex cells mostly did not, so
  a cert comparison on such a docket partly measured fetch ability. On the
  2026-10-05 predict runs, 16 flags on 14 cert cases named a companion, lead
  or held-for petition outside the record as the decisive signal.

  **What moved.** `provision-snapshot`, for a cell that names its `--event`,
  reads the docket numbers its **placed** snapshot links
  (`provision.vide_docket_numbers`, at most four, in served order, each
  shaped as a SCOTUS docket number). It reads them after the cell's gates and
  placement, so a refused cell reads none. It resolves them in one scan of
  the live slice of the index (`corpus.live_scotus_case_ids_by_docket_numbers`)
  and stages each one's latest stored snapshot as
  `record/related/<docket number>.json`, with `related.json` listing every
  link and the reason any was not staged. Under the `casestore` backend the
  production fleet provisions under, the scan runs over the ordinary read
  backend, as the row gate's does, and the snapshot comes from the content
  store. Each companion is cut by the date rule (`provision.place_related`):
  - strictly before the cell's cutoff;
  - on the interim arrival moment, strictly before its opening day, since the
    cell's own docket is cut at the opening entry and a companion has no
    anchor to cut at;
  - on a forward cell with no cutoff, strictly before the cell's own snapshot
    date, because a companion pulled later than the cell's docket could carry
    an order disposing of both, which the cell's own terminal gate never read.

  Each is then redacted as the back-test redacts (`provision.redact_snapshot`),
  since a companion is always rebuilt from a later payload and its undated
  top-level fields outlive the cut: `QPLink` exists only once certiorari is
  granted, and the counsel blocks grow with a grant's amici. The redaction
  removes the party and counsel blocks, and with them any contact detail. A
  replay cell with no cutoff gets none. An evaluate cell (no `--event`) and an
  `--out` copy read none. `local-cascade` stages them the same way. The cert
  back-test's replay provisioner, which stages no documents either, is
  unchanged.

  **A residual, stated.** A `truncated` placement keeps the latest payload's
  `RelatedCaseNumber`, which is undated, so a link the Court added after the
  cell's moment (a petition later held for another) can be read on such a
  cell. A `dated` placement reads the links as the docket served them.

  No prompt byte and no registry field moves in the carrying change, so no
  digest moves there: `uv run fedcourts process-digest --all` prints
  `proc-v10` and the six digests `605201bd…` (claude-baseline), `7ab92dd4…`
  (codex-baseline), `bee46e92…` (gemini-baseline), `167b7d71…`
  (claude-judge), `a8610eec…` (codex-judge) and `6a88d3dc…` (gemini-judge),
  identical with and without it. The predict prompt's paragraph naming
  `record/related/` is carried by the re-bless that registers the moments

  **A harness boundary under the 2026-10-11 pooled rule.** The change adds to

  - **The registry row.** The boundary is `vide-related-dockets`:
    `HarnessBoundary("vide-related-dockets", <carrying promotion merge hash>,

- **The cert resolver reads a direct appeal's summary affirmance and its
  dismissals; recorded 2026-10-22.** The other side of the 2026-10-19
  direct-appeal entry, in the same classes: a **scoring-baseline** entry and a
  **conditioning** one through the same numbers. It moves the realized cert
  record of mandatory-jurisdiction direct appeals, which the statpack's
  per-band segment pools are built from, and those pools are what a cert cell
  is provisioned with and stamped against. That earlier entry is not otherwise
  edited. It moves no digest: no prompt template, neither agent config and not
  `src/fedcourtsai/process_version.py` changes, and `uv run fedcourts
  process-digest --all` prints `proc-v10` and the same six digests at this
  change as at its parent (`605201bd…`, `7ab92dd4…`, `bee46e92…`,
  `167b7d71…`, `a8610eec…`, `6a88d3dc…`). It registers one harness boundary,
  below. The carrying merge writes nothing to the corpus or the ledger.

  **The pattern change** (`src/fedcourtsai/pipeline/cert_signals.py`). A
  second table, `_DIRECT_APPEAL_EXIT_SIGNALS`, is scanned after every
  existing row, so the plenary-review rows and every cert row keep their
  readings and win wherever they match the same entry. Its rows and labels:
  - "The appeal is dismissed for want of a substantial federal question."
    (with or without "properly presented") → `dismissed`;
  - "Appeal dismissed for want of jurisdiction." / "The appeal is dismissed
    for want of jurisdiction." (or "lack of jurisdiction") → `dismissed`;
  - "The appeal is DISMISSED AS MOOT." → `dismissed`, on the `mootness`
    basis, as a cert dismissal as moot carries;
  - "Motion to affirm GRANTED." → `denied`;
  - a summary affirmance, "Adjudged to be AFFIRMED.", "Judgment AFFIRMED.",
    "The judgment [of the … Court] is affirmed." → `denied`.

  **Why these labels.** The `Disposition` convention already puts summary
  affirmance and want-of-a-question on the denied/dismissed side, and both
  labels sit in every resolved denominator and outside the grant family, so
  the pools read each exit as a not-granted resolution either way. The label
  is chosen by what the order does. A summary affirmance (and the motion to
  affirm it grants) declines plenary review and leaves the judgment below
  standing, which is what a cert denial records, so it reads `denied` and
  dates `date_cert_denied` with the termination, as a cert denial does. A
  dismissal is the Court's own word for an appeal it disposes of without
  reaching the merits, so it reads `dismissed` and dates the termination
  alone. The dismissal rows are scanned before the affirmance rows, so an
  entry that dismisses one part and affirms another reads `dismissed`. Both
  are the not-granted side, so the order moves only the label axis.

  **No merits judgment latches on a summary affirmance.** The live channel
  latches `merits_judgment` only on a grant that opens a merits proceeding
  (`MERITS_PROCEEDING_DISPOSITIONS`), and `denied` is not one, so a summary
  affirmance carries no merits pair. No merits event is minted
  (`outcome._merits_mint_verdict` returns no verdict without a
  merits-opening grant), and the statpack's merits section and its baseline,
  which admit only merits-opening grants, do not read these rows. That is the
  conservative call: the merits population is the briefed-and-argued one,
  and a summary affirmance is not in it.

  **Guarding against the merits judgment.** "Judgment AFFIRMED." is also how
  a merits judgment reads after argument on a granted cert docket, so the
  entry alone cannot say which it is. The exit table is therefore never read
  by an entry-level reader. Only `docket_disposition_signals` opens it, per
  entry, under two tests on the docket:
  - **direct-appeal context**: some entry carries a jurisdictional statement,
    a statement as to jurisdiction, or a motion to affirm or to dismiss or
    affirm, papers only an appeal carries;
  - **no plenary review yet**: no earlier entry shows argument ("Argued."),
    a setting for argument, merits briefing, or a joint appendix.

  Each row also reads only where its phrase opens its sentence and the
  sentence names no docket number. That is the 2026-10-19 cross-docket guard,
  extended to the new rows, so "The appeal in No. 17-2 is dismissed …" never
  disposes of the docket whose entry carries it. An entry naming an opinion of
  the Court or a per curiam opinion is not read. The existing order guards run
  on every match, with one exception: the motion-to-affirm row is exempt from
  the motion-opening guard, because its subject is the motion it decides.

  The docket-level readers are ingest-time resolution (`ingest._live_resolution`),
  the historical loader's keep/skip read (and so `refresh_dockets`), the
  disposition basis, the reachability probe, and the forward-leakage guard.
  Every entry-level reader keeps the cert table alone: the convergence sweep,
  the refused-sentence readers, `cert_grant_date`, and the before-the-
  first-disposition moment readers. The convergence sweep's population is
  `granted` rows and exits on rows recording a grant, so it never reaches
  these rows.

  Deliberate misses:
  - a split order ("Adjudged to be AFFIRMED in part and REVERSED in part.",
    a dismissal "with respect to" one district beside an affirmance as to
    another);
  - "affirmed by an equally divided Court";
  - a bare "Appeal dismissed." that names no basis.

- **`proc-v11`: the predict prompt names the sg-brief, first-relist and
  post-argument moments, which the fan-out now forecasts; recorded
  2026-10-22.** Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-23` (merge
  `fd98eda9327806f1a0eed032377e05e480c6c33e`, `2026-10-23T02:37:11Z`), to be tagged
  **`prereg/proc-v11`**. Registered under the merge-stamped rule, so its
  counting instant, its three bless moments and every window edge it moves
  are the carrying merge's committer time. It is the third supersession
  shape for all three predictors at once
  ([process-version.md](process-version.md#freezing-the-cutover-procedure)):
  `.github/prompts/predict.md`, which every predictor digest reads, changes,
  so each predictor's open window **closes** at this label's instant and a
  `proc-v11` window opens there for each new digest. No evaluator digest
  moves: neither the evaluate prompt nor any judge's config changes, so the
  three judges carry their bless moments forward and add this label to their
  blessing labels. Nothing is de-counted and nothing is re-owed: every cell
  counted in a closed window keeps counting under its own label.

  **What moved, in the predict prompt.**
  - *Stage: cert* lists five moments rather than three. `moment: sg-brief`
    (`evt-brief-sg-disposition`, opened the day the Solicitor General's
    invited brief is filed) tells the cell to read
    `record/documents/sg-invited-brief.txt`, state the recommendation and
    how far it follows it, and anchor on the statpack's CVSG cut, which no
    committed table splits by the recommendation. `moment: relist`
    (`evt-order-relist-disposition`, opened on the first relist) says the
    cell's `band` and `distribution_count` already include the relist, keeps
    the band anchoring every cert cell uses, and names the relist-count cut,
    pooled from bucket 1 up, as a cross-check that, like the band, counts a
    reschedule as a relist and so likely reads low for this population. The claim-masking paragraph adds that `cvsg-increment` is
    vacuous on an sg-brief cell and that `relist-increment` on a relist cell
    asks for a second relist.
  - *Stage: merits* lists three moments rather than two. `moment: argued`
    (`evt-argument-judgment`, opened on the argument day the Court's
    transcript list gives) tells the cell to read
    `record/documents/argument-transcript.txt`, to summarize rather than
    quote, and to say how far it reads a question from the bench as a lean.
    A forward merits cell that retrieves what a later moment adds (the
    argument, on a grant or briefed cell run after it) is told to say so.
    The paragraph on scoring the moments separately is written for three.
    The anchor rule's grant-Term instruction now takes the grant date from
    the docket's grant order, since a later moment's `opened_at` is the
    brief or the argument rather than the grant.
  - The claim-set paragraph names the new moments under `cert-v2` and
    `merits-v1`.
  - Input item 5 gains the paragraph describing `record/related/`, which the
    2026-10-22 `vide-related-dockets` entry deferred to this label so that
    the predictor digests move once, and the older debts listed under *The
    amendment debt* below.

  **What moved, in the code.** `pipeline/moments.py` sets `forecastable` on
  the three moments, so the fan-out admits their open events. The relist and
  sg-brief moments each forecast the next conference (the one the petition
  was relisted for, the first one after the brief), so the cert admission
  (`store._cert_forecastable`) refuses a cell on either once a conference the
  petition was distributed for on or after the trigger has sat on it by the
  plan day and left it undecided
  (`cert_signals.conference_sat_since`): such a petition has been relisted
  again or held, and a cell placed back at the trigger would be scored as the
  population it has left. The reading of "sat" is the distribution
  moment's: a conference day counts as sat, a petition taken off the
  conference by a call for response or a reschedule was not considered, and
  a live payload stored before the conference, no readable payload, an event
  with no opening date, or a relist whose own distribution entry the payload
  does not carry, refuses. The
  call-for-response moment stays declared and switched off: its first polls
  open events for petitions called for a response long before, and how those
  back-dated events count is not decided here. `pull.REPREDICT_MOMENTS` does
  not change, so none of the three is re-owed when a later label de-counts
  its cells: the argued moment is held out with the other merits moments as
  a funding decision, and a relist or sg-brief re-predict would be spend on a
  cohort that has not yet run, and would need the conference bound above on
  the re-predict path too.

  **The three populations, pre-registered here.** Each is scored on its own
  `<stage>@<moment>` population and never pooled with another moment's
  ([metrics/README.md](../metrics/README.md)).
  - `cert@sg-brief`: open petitions on which the Solicitor General filed the
    brief a CVSG invited, opened on the brief's docket date. It declares
    `cert-v2`; its `disposition` claim scores against the frozen band's
    strictly-prior reached rate, as every cert moment's does. That baseline
    does not see the Solicitor General's recommendation, the strongest
    single cert signal, so positive skill against it is expected of any rule
    that follows the recommendation: a `cert@sg-brief` figure against the
    band is not a claim of skill beyond the recommendation, and none is made
    until a committed cut splits the population by it. The cell's cutoff is
    the day after the brief; it is refused (exit 5) where neither the dated
    stored snapshot nor the latest payload cut to the moment carries the
    brief's entry, and is not minted once the first conference after the
    brief has sat.
  - `cert@relist`: open petitions at their first relist, which is a later
    distribution of the petition, entered after a conference that sat on it
    and within the relist window, naming a later conference. It declares
    `cert-v2` and scores against the same band baseline. The band is built
    from the distribution count, which takes in a reschedule before the first
    conference as well as a true relist, so the baseline is measured on a
    looser membership than this moment's and likely reads low for it: skill
    on this population reads favourably by an unmeasured amount, and a
    figure says so. Its `relist-increment` claim resolves on any further
    distribution, a reschedule included; the relist increment has no run-day
    mask, which is harmless while the claim has no baseline and so no score,
    and is owed before a per-Term relist cut gives it one. It is placed and
    refused on the same terms as the sg-brief moment, and is not minted once
    the conference it was relisted for has sat.
  - `merits@argued`: granted cases with an open merits proceeding whose
    argument transcript the live poll has latched, opened on the argument
    day. It declares `merits-v1` and scores against the strictly-prior
    disturbed rate, as both other merits moments do. Its cells alone are
    handed the transcript (`provision.documents_for_moment`).

  No base rate is re-priced and no membership rule moves for any existing
  population.

  **Events opened before the carrying merge.** The live poll has minted these
  moments' events, switched off, since their declaring changes reached
  `main`, so the first rounds after the carrying merge place cells on events
  opened before it, with a placement lag the placed-cell rule already owes
  beside a figure ([metrics/README.md](../metrics/README.md)). The conference
  bound keeps a relist or sg-brief cell to a petition whose next conference
  has not yet sat, so such a cell forecasts the same conference a timely one
  would; on the argued moment nothing material happens between argument and
  judgment. Even so, any figure over one of the three populations states
  beside it how many of its cells sit on events opened before the carrying
  merge, and is quoted with and without them until the populations hold
  cells on events opened after it.

  **No cross-moment figure is registered here.** The prompt tells a cell
  that a difference between its moments' forecasts is what the later
  evidence was worth. No figure of that kind is pre-registered by this
  entry, and none is a claim until a dated entry fixes its form (the same
  predictor and window, paired by event, a Brier difference with its `n`).

- **A predict cell's context freezes its docket's `Vide` links, and the board
  cuts the forward stratum by them; recorded 2026-10-22.** A
  **reading-rule** change with a conditioning half, recorded before any
  outcome the cut reads.

  **Why.** A forecast on a held petition, a cross-petition or a companion
  case may depend on another docket's course. A held petition's grant-side
  mass is mostly a hold-then-GVR route. Nothing on the board told those
  forecasts apart, so a pooled figure could not show whether linked dockets
  score differently.

  **The conditioning half.** `PredictionContext` gains `vide_links`: the
  docket numbers the provisioned payload links as `Vide`, read by the same
  rule that stages them under `record/related/` (own number dropped, at most
  four, in the Court's order). The value is an empty list where a live-shape
  payload links nothing, and null where the payload is not the live shape. The
  cell reads `record/context.json`, so the field joins its information set.
  It adds nothing the cell could not already read: the same list is in the
  payload's `RelatedCaseNumber`, and each linked docket the corpus holds is
  staged under `record/related/`. No prompt text or other digest input changes, so no
  digest moves.
  - **The registry row.** The boundary is `context-vide-links`. It applies to
    every predictor, with reach `all`, and is not gradual: every cell
    provisioned after the carrying merge freezes the field. It is registered
    **pending** in this change's own PR (`fedcourts register-boundary`). Its
    `merge` and `at` stay null until the promotion merge that carries it to
    `main` stamps them (`promotion-record`).

  **The reading rule.** Each cert entry's forward stratum, and each later
  cert moment's stage entry, carries `by_link`. The cut has three keys:
  - `linked`: the scored prediction's frozen `vide_links` names a docket;
  - `unlinked`: it names none;
  - `(none)`: it froze no list. This holds every prediction made before the
    carrying merge.

  The cut is built as `by_band` is, over the same cells and skill terms, and
  the blocks' `evaluations` sum to the forward stratum's.
  - **Descriptive only.** It is never a rank key or a headline. It has no
    paired filing, so no ordering of engines within a key may be read off it.
    It carries no set-aside sensitivity line, and `release-sensitivity` does
    not project it. `linked` is a different population from `unlinked`: its
    grant-side outcomes run through hold-then-GVR, and the band anchor was not
    pooled for it, so the two blocks are not a like-for-like comparison.
  - **Not before its cells exist.** The `linked` and `unlinked` blocks read
    only cells provisioned after the carrying merge. Until those cells are
    graded, each entry's whole forward stratum files under `(none)`.
  - **Expected population.** Measured over the production blob `6701546c…`
    (the `origin/main` pointer at `6d56d6a9f`): 7 of the 134 open queued live
    rows link one `Vide` docket each, and 15 of the 372 queued rows overall.
    The blob's `corpus-info` vintage was not recorded when it was read, so
    a later blob may count differently. Either way, `linked` stays a small
    block, and a figure on it may not be read without its `evaluations`.

  **What it moves.** No scored figure: the pooled strata, the ranks, `paired`
  and every floor field are unchanged. Once cells sit on both sides of the
  stamped boundary, each pooled entry's and each paired engine's `boundaries`
  list gains a `context-vide-links` row. That row is composition, not a cut.
  The `(none)` block of a board built after the merge equals its forward
  stratum until a post-merge cell is graded.

  Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-23` (merge commit

- **A predict cell's context freezes whether its docket's filings are on
  paper only; recorded 2026-10-23.** A **conditioning** change with no
  reading rule and no scored figure.

  **Why.** Under Rule 34.6 and Paragraph 9 of the Court's electronic filing
  guidelines, some dockets file on paper only, and the Court posts nothing
  behind those filings. These are mostly immigration and detention cases, and
  the Solicitor General is often a party. A cell on one gets an empty
  `record/documents/`. Cells read that as a provisioning failure and flagged
  it: 13 cells over 9 predict runs, 2026-10-03 to 10-17, counted from the
  agent-flag roll-ups on the agent-feedback tracking issue. The pipeline
  already counted this class as the back-fill's `no_link` floor. Nothing in a
  cell's record said so.

  **The conditioning half.** `PredictionContext` gains `paper_only_filings`,
  read off the placed payload in docket order:
  - `true` where the payload carries the Court's paper-only entry, with no
    later entry quoting the rule to call for electronic versions (the Court
    makes that call once briefing and argument are scheduled);
  - `false` where the payload carries neither entry, or the lift follows the
    paper-only entry;
  - null where the payload has no `ProceedingsandOrder` list: the REST
    shape, or a cut that dropped the list because no moment could be placed.

  A `truncated` payload answers as at its cut. The cell reads
  `record/context.json`, so the field joins its information set. It adds
  nothing the cell could not already read, because the entry is in the staged
  snapshot. No prompt text or other digest input changes, so no digest moves.
  Telling cells in the prompt that this is expected is left for the next
  re-bless. The cert back-test's replay contexts are built by the same
  builder and carry the field too, though those cells stage no documents at
  all.
  - **The registry row.** The boundary is `context-paper-only-filings`. It
    applies to every predictor, with reach `all`, and is not gradual: every
    cell provisioned after the carrying merge freezes the field. It is
    registered **pending** in this change's own PR
    (`fedcourts register-boundary`). Its `merge` and `at` stay null until the
    promotion merge that carries it to `main` stamps them
    (`promotion-record`).
  - **Expected population.** Read directly from the production per-case
    content store on 2026-10-23, not from a pulled index blob, over each
    case's newest stored snapshot (the newest dated 2026-10-23). It covered the 285
    SCOTUS cases holding a prediction run in September or October 2026. The
    reader marks 7 of them `true`, and each of the 7 has no stored document. Two
    more carry the paper-only entry followed by the lift; they read `false`
    and hold stored filings (4 and 7).

  **What it moves.** No scored figure. Once cells sit on both sides of the
  stamped boundary, each pooled entry's and each paired engine's `boundaries`
  list gains a `context-paper-only-filings` row. That row is composition, not
  a cut. The field is no cut, exclusion or rank key on any board. A later
  dated entry must register one before any figure reads it.

  Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-25` (merge commit
  `51cca3cb5eab4d7fa8ab3701f1dbae103d1a00c0`, merged `2026-10-25T13:40:46Z`).

  The runnable effect check once it is live:
  - `uv run pytest tests/test_paper_only_filings.py` is green;
  - on the first predict run's collect PR after the carrying merge, `jq -c
    '.context | has("paper_only_filings")' data/cases/scotus/*/events/*/predictions/*/<run_id>/prediction.json`
    prints `true` for every file;
  - on `main`, `uv run python -c
    "from fedcourtsai.process_version import HARNESS_BOUNDARIES as H;
    print('context-paper-only-filings' in {b.name for b in H})"` prints `True`

- **The questions-presented cut opens at the petition's real heading, drops
  page folios, and marks a capped section; recorded 2026-10-23.** A change to
  a cell input and to the QP-topic labeler's input, with no reading rule and
  no scored figure.

  **Why.** The stored `questions-presented` row is what a cert cell reads as
  `record/documents/questions-presented.txt`, and what the QP-topic labeler
  labels. Agent flags named five bad rows. Read from the stored petition text,
  they come from four faults:
  - pypdf recovered a small-caps heading as "QUESTION S PRESENTED", which the
    start rule missed. The cut then opened at prose ("the questions presented
    are:") or at an argument heading that spells the phrase. On 73280982 the
    row held printed pages 31 to 33 of the argument.
  - A "Questions to Review" heading was not read at all, so no row was stored.
  - The page folio before the next heading ("ii") was kept as the row's last
    line.
  - A section longer than the 4,000-character cap was cut there, but the row
    was stored with `truncated: false`.

  The fifth flag (73331499, "cut mid-Q2") is the filing's own text: the
  petition's second question ends mid-sentence.

  **The change.**
  - The start rule reads `QUESTION\s?S?\s+PRESENTED`, and absorbs a heading's
    `FOR REVIEW` tail.
  - A `Questions to Review` or `Question for Review` heading opens the section
    only where it stands alone on its line. Prose and argument headings say
    those words too.
  - A lone folio on the section's last line is dropped.
  - A section cut at the cap is stored with `truncated: true`.
  - `backfill-questions-presented` re-derives stored rows from their stored
    petition text, as it does after any cutter change. A row whose text is
    unchanged but whose cap mark is wrong is rewritten under its own reason
    class, `cap-mark`. A rewrite that only drops a `FOR REVIEW` tail or a
    trailing folio is classed `trim-only`, so the dry run sets the mechanical
    trims apart from the rows a maintainer reads.
  - New rows take the cut at ingest.
  - **The registry row.** The boundary is `qp-cutter-split-and-review-headings`.
    It applies to every predictor, with reach `all`, and is **gradual**: stored
    rows change only when a maintainer-dispatched back-fill applies. It is
    registered pending in this change's own PR (`fedcourts register-boundary`).
    The promotion merge that carries it stamps it (`promotion-record`).

  **Measured effect.** The current and the new extractor were each run over
  the stored petition text of every live-slice SCOTUS case. The read went
  directly to the production per-case content store on 2026-10-23, with the
  case list taken from the index blob `2c899403…` (latest pull 2026-10-23,
  latest snapshot row 2026-07-13). Of 25,914 live-slice cases, 9,859 carry
  petition text and 8,755 of those carry a QP heading under either rule; 6,446
  derive a different section.

  | Class | Rows |
  | --- | ---: |
  | Only a trailing page folio dropped | 5,624 |
  | Folio and a leading `FOR REVIEW` dropped | 430 |
  | Only a leading `FOR REVIEW` dropped | 297 |
  | Reopened at the real heading (mostly the split heading) | 70 |
  | Heading now found where none was read | 18 |
  | Empty before, now derived | 5 |
  | Heading now found, nothing usable under it | 2 |
  | Derived before, now empty | 0 |

  The 18 newly found sections were read by hand: each opens on the petition's
  questions or the preface to them, 13 under a review heading standing alone
  on its line and 5 under the split heading. Of the 70 reopened rows, 56 were
  checked mechanically: the old text, whitespace-normalised and with the tail
  and folio trimmed, lies inside the new section. The other 14 were read by
  hand: each old row was argument prose cut at the cap or at a phrase, and each
  new row is the petition's questions. No row loses a question.

  A dry run of the back-fill's own classification against the rows as stored
  gives the triage list to expect: 6,348 `trim-only`, 71 `other-change`, 261
  `cap-mark`, 20 `derived-anew`, 4 `prose-terminator-fragment`, 3 each of
  `below-floor`, `stale-toc-fragment` and `toc-junk-emptied`, 45 refused, and
  3,101 unchanged. The 45 refused rows and 8 rewrites (the 3
  `toc-junk-emptied`, the 3 `stale-toc-fragment` and 2 of the
  `prose-terminator-fragment`) differ from the stored row under the current
  extractor too: stored rows an earlier back-fill has not converged, not this
  change's effect. A capped row's `truncated` mark reaches the cell through
  `record/documents/documents.json`, so the 261 `cap-mark` rows change a cell
  input though their text does not.
  - **The labeler.** The QP-topic labels already committed were read off the
    rows as stored. A batch labeled after the back-fill applies reads the new
    rows, so a QP whose row changed class "reopened" or "newly derived" can
    label differently from a batch before it. Folio and `FOR REVIEW` drops
    change no question text.

  **What it moves.** No scored figure and no digest: no prompt or other digest
  input changes. Once cells sit on both sides of the stamped boundary, each
  pooled entry's and each paired engine's `boundaries` list gains a
  `qp-cutter-split-and-review-headings` row, which is composition, not a cut.

  `51cca3cb5eab4d7fa8ab3701f1dbae103d1a00c0`, merged `2026-10-25T13:40:46Z`).

  - after the carrying merge, a `run-repair` dry run with `repair:
    qp-backfill` reports about 6,700 rows to rewrite: about 6,350

- **`proc-v12`: the predict prompt elicits the authorship forecasts, and every
  declared moment names its stage's authorship set; recorded 2026-10-23.**
  Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-25` (merge `51cca3cb5eab4d7fa8ab3701f1dbae103d1a00c0`,
  `2026-10-25T13:40:46Z`), to be tagged **`prereg/proc-v12`**. Registered under
  the merge-stamped rule, so its counting instant, its three bless moments and
  every window edge it moves are the carrying merge's committer time. It is
  the third supersession shape for all three predictors at once
  ([process-version.md](process-version.md#freezing-the-cutover-procedure)):
  `.github/prompts/predict.md`, which every predictor digest reads, changes,
  so each predictor's open `proc-v11` window **closes** at this label's
  instant and a `proc-v12` window opens there for each new digest. No
  evaluator digest moves: neither the evaluate prompt nor any judge's config
  changes, so the three judges carry their bless moments forward and add this
  label to their blessing labels. Nothing is de-counted and nothing is
  re-owed: every cell counted in a closed window keeps counting under its own
  label, scored under the set it was asked.

  **What moved, in the predict prompt.**
  - *Stage: merits* replaces the sentence telling a cell that authorship
    resolves against nothing with the `merits-v2` set: the binary
    `judgment-disturbed` claim, unchanged, and two distribution claims in
    `claim_distributions`, `majority-author` (one distribution over the bench
    sitting on the snapshot date and `per-curiam`, summing to 1) and
    `separate-writers` (per Justice, each probability on its own), both
    scored. The cell is told the baselines are strictly-prior Term history,
    so restating it is worth zero, and to give its reasons in the forecast
    document.
  - *Stage: cert* and *Stage: interim* name `cert-v3` and `interim-v2` and
    add `order-writers` (per Justice: the chance each sitting Justice writes
    on the disposing order), banked and never scored. The
    `dissent-from-denial` claim is unchanged and stays the cert stage's
    scored writing claim.
  - The `prediction.json` field list gains `claim_distributions`: the labels
    (sitting Justices as the roster spells them, plus `per-curiam` on
    `majority-author` alone), the sitting bench by name with the date it last
    changed, the sum rule, no additions and no declining, and that the block
    rides `claims`. A writer is an author or co-signing author; joining
    another Justice's writing is not writing one, as the writing roles the
    claims resolve against record it.

  **What moved, in the code.** `pipeline/moments.py` points the six cert
  moments at `cert-v3`, the three interim moments at `interim-v2` and the
  three merits moments at `merits-v2`. Each carries its predecessor's binary
  claims unchanged and in the same order. A cell stamped under a label before
  this one (`process_version.AUTHORSHIP_CLAIMS_FROM`), or unstamped and
  stating no distribution block, was asked the predecessor set and is scored
  under it (`pipeline.claims.declared_claim_set_for`), so the moment table's
  advance relabels no committed grading. An absent distribution block is
  masked, as an absent `claims` block is; `validate` reports a block naming
  a claim its set does not declare, and checks a distribution block stated
  without a `claims` block. The offline stub states an even split, so the
  cascade smoke exercises the block. The authorship tally
  (`record/authorship-tally.json`) stays withheld from cells
  (`provision.AUTHORSHIP_TALLY_WITHHELD`): this label releases no new input.

  **The populations, pre-registered here.** The authorship rows sit in
  `ClaimScoreBlock.distributions`, never in a binary total, and are read per
  `<stage>@<moment>` population, never pooled across moments
  ([metrics/README.md](../metrics/README.md)).
  - `majority-author` and `separate-writers` on `merits@grant`,
    `merits@briefed` and `merits@argued`, resolved as *The authorship claims*
    in [outcome-decomposition.md](outcome-decomposition.md) states:
    `majority-author` only on an argued decision whose stamped author agrees
    with the docket's decision method, `separate-writers` only where the
    writing roles were observed.
  - `order-writers` on every cert and interim moment, resolved and banked,
    never scored and never quoted as skill. A scored form, if one is ever
    registered, is a new set version and scores only cells asked under it;
    the banked cells stay unscored.

  **The baseline constants, registered here.** Both scored claims' baselines
  (`pipeline.base_rates`) pool the statpack's authorship section over the
  October Terms strictly before the cell's, inside the salience lookback band
  (`salience.base_rate_lookback_terms`, **10** Terms in `config/tracking.yaml`,
  and never before OT2020, where the per-opinion record starts):
  - a baseline is `None`, and its claim unscored, below **30** pooled
    decisions (`AUTHORSHIP_BASE_RATE_MIN_DECISIONS`): argued decisions for
    the author, observed ones for separate writing;
  - each Justice's rate is shrunk toward the even split (author) or the
    bench-wide pooled rate (separate writing) by **20** pseudo-decisions
    (`AUTHORSHIP_PRIOR_WEIGHT`);
  - the per-curiam share is **(per curiams + 0.5) / (argued decisions + 1)**,
    so a window that saw no per curiam still prices one above zero, and the
    signed remainder is scaled so the author baseline sums to 1.

  None of the three was chosen against an outcome a merits-v2 cell will be
  scored on: no cell has been asked the forecast, and no committed merits
  outcome carries a stamped author.

  **Owed before any `majority-author` figure is quoted.**
  - The census *Why the author resolves from its own stamp* names: stamped
    merits outcomes masked for an unclassified or disagreeing decision
    method, by stamped kind (signed, per curiam). It can be taken only after
    the opinions writer's first `opinion-votes` apply stamps `merits_author`
    across the merits population, which follows this promotion. Until a dated
    entry quotes it, a `majority-author` figure is not a claim. If the census
    shows the method classification masking one kind more often than the
    other, the remedy is a new set version with a changed mask, applied to
    cells asked under it; `merits-v2` cells already graded are never
    re-masked.
  - The baseline and the resolved pool differ where signed decisions go
    unclassified (*Baselines* in
    [outcome-decomposition.md](outcome-decomposition.md)); a figure states
    the per-curiam share of its resolved rows beside the baseline's.

  **What this label does not register.** No late-Term authorship moment:
  `fedcourts authorship-tally` reads the pattern, but no moment declares it
  and the tally stays out of cells, and the moment still owes the eight
  tests ([milestones.md](milestones.md)). No authorship figure is
  pre-registered as a headline: the rows are diagnostic, and the
  `majority-author` rows are not quoted at all until the census lands.

  **The amendment debt this label leaves.** The evaluate prompt still names
  the interim and merits sets by their predecessors' ids (`interim-v1`,
  `merits-v1`) where it tells a judge the `claim_scores` block is the
  harness's. The instruction it carries, that the judge neither fills nor
  corrects the block, holds under the new ids, and editing it would move all
  three evaluator digests, which this label holds. It is paid at the next
  label that moves them.

- **Head-cut petitions, applications and appendices are re-cut the
  appendix-aware way, a slice at a time; recorded 2026-10-24.** A change to
  what cells are given, under unchanged digests, with no reading rule and no
  scored figure.

  **Why.** The appendix-aware cut, carried by `promotion/2026-10-10` (entry
  above), applies to rows stored under it. Fetching is idempotent per kind and
  URL, so a `petition`, `application` or `appendix` row stored before it keeps
  the plain head cut while its link is unchanged: the 150,000-character cap
  lands inside the appendix, the lower-court decisions after the first long one
  are dropped, and nothing in the text says so. That entry recorded the
  residue; nothing converged it.

  **The change.** A dispatched pass, `fedcourts recut-documents`, run as
  `run-repair`'s `recut` selector value (*Contract for the re-cut pass* in
  [live-sources.md](live-sources.md)):
  - The class is every stored row of the three kinds that is `truncated`, not
    `ocr_derived`, carries no `[pipeline note:` line and has one Court URL,
    over the predict-relevant live-slice rows, or the whole live slice with
    the `all-live` option. OCR-recovered rows keep their head cut by design.
  - Each candidate is re-fetched by its stored URL and re-cut by the fetching
    lanes' own `extract_filing_text`. A PDF whose page count differs from the
    stored row's, or whose re-cut does not open with the stored text, is
    skipped as another filing. A re-cut row keeps its kind,
    URL and entry date and takes the new text, pages, truncation flag and the
    apply's date as `fetched_at`.
  - A re-cut petition's questions-presented row is rewritten only where the
    re-cut moves the derived section and the stored row is the stored text's
    own derivation; one a cutter change left behind is
    `backfill-questions-presented`'s. Over the 25 petitions of the dry run
    below, none was rewritten.
  - New rows already take the cut at ingest; nothing about them changes.

  **What it moves.** No digest: no prompt or other digest input changes. A
  cell provisioned after an apply over a case it re-cut reads a different
  `petition.txt`, `application.txt` or `appendix.txt` from a cell provisioned
  before it on the same case, inside the open windows. The text a cell reads
  changes after the filing's own body, which both cuts keep, or, where the body
  alone fills the cap, only at its end; either way the new text states each
  cut in a note. No scored figure, cut, exclusion or rank key reads which cut a
  cell was given.
  - **The registry row.** The boundary is `recut-head-cut-documents`. It
    applies to every predictor, with reach `all`, and is **gradual**: stored
    rows change only when a maintainer-dispatched apply reaches them, so a
    cell after it may still read the head cut. It is registered pending in
    this change's own PR (`fedcourts register-boundary`). The promotion merge
    that carries it stamps it (`promotion-record`). Which rows each apply
    replaced is its own ledger: its `<case_id> <kind>: RE-CUT …` lines in the
    `run-repair` run summary, which a reader splitting cells by document
    vintage reads beside each cell's `provisioned_at`.

  **Expected population.** Read from corpus blob `9d209a20…` (latest pull
  2026-10-24, latest snapshot row 2026-07-13) with its per-case content store,
  on 2026-10-24: 548 rows in the predict-relevant scope (540 petitions, 8
  applications, no appendix), of 2,707 stored rows of the three kinds over
  3,708 predict-relevant live-slice rows. 90 of them (83 petitions, 7
  applications) sit on rows queued for prediction; the other 458 on rows
  selected by the salience gate alone. Their `fetched_at` runs 2026-07-12 to
  2026-10-09. Left out as truncated but not candidates: 53 rows already
  carrying a cut note and 2 OCR-derived rows, and no unfetchable URL. Over the whole live slice
  (`all-live`) the class is 1,201 (1,193 petitions, 8 applications) of 10,025
  stored rows over 25,961 live-slice rows, with 60 noted and 14 OCR-derived
  rows left out.
  A bounded dry run (`--max-cases 25`) re-fetched the first 25 candidates,
  all petitions: all 25 re-cut, none `pages-changed`, `head-changed`,
  `unreadable`, `unchanged` or failed, 1 to 10 cut notes each.

  Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-25` (merge commit
  `51cca3cb5eab4d7fa8ab3701f1dbae103d1a00c0`, merged `2026-10-25T13:40:46Z`).

  - `uv run pytest tests/test_document_recut.py` is green;
  - after the carrying merge, a `run-repair` dry run with `repair: recut` and

    all `recut` in its per-kind outcome lines. Its apply is the maintainer's
    dispatch, and the re-walk the step makes afterwards must report the
    class less what the apply re-cut.

- **`proc-v13`: the predict prompt tells cells about the inputs stored for
  them, and provisioning hands them over; recorded 2026-10-24.**
  Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-26` (merge `728efab06a9ad44bf39523c7181827d4eade70de`,
  `2026-10-26T19:00:50Z`), to be tagged **`prereg/proc-v13`**. Registered under
  the merge-stamped rule, so its counting instant, its three bless moments and
  every window edge it moves are the carrying merge's committer time. It is
  the third supersession shape for all three predictors at once
  ([process-version.md](process-version.md#freezing-the-cutover-procedure)):
  `.github/prompts/predict.md` changes, so each predictor's open `proc-v12`
  window **closes** at this label's instant and a `proc-v13` window opens
  there for each new digest. No evaluator digest moves, so the three judges
  carry their bless moments forward and add this label to their blessing
  labels. Nothing is de-counted and nothing is re-owed: every cell counted in
  a closed window keeps counting under its own label.

  **Why a label for inputs the digest does not see.** A process digest covers
  the prompt bytes and the canonical config, not provisioning code, so a newly
  staged input would change what a cell reads under an unchanged digest. Each
  input below was stored first and held back, and is released here, in the
  label whose prompt tells cells what it is and how to read it.

  **What cells are handed from this label on.**
  - *Documents* (`provision.WITHHELD_KINDS` is now empty): on a cert docket,
    `supplemental-brief.txt` (every party's Rule 15.8 supplemental brief while
    the petition is pending) and `party-letter.txt` (the parties' letters to
    the Clerk bearing on the case); on a granted docket,
    `merits-amicus-united-states.txt` (the United States' amicus brief on the
    merits). Each is cut to the cell's cutoff as every other kind is.
  - *Argument features*: a post-argument cell's
    `record/argument-features.json`, the deterministic parse of the transcript
    it was staged (`provision.staged_argument_features`).
  - *Two statpack sections*: the cert amicus-brief cut over the paid scored
    segment (`Cert petitions by amicus-brief count`, buckets `0`, `1`, `2+`),
    and the per-Justice merits votes section (`justice_votes`), each Term's
    complete lineups rolled up by `pipeline.justice_priors`. The amicus cut
    reads the `cert_amicus_briefs` column, whose resolved history the
    `cert-amicus-rederive` repair pass fills. Its apply ran on 2026-10-25
    (`run-repair` run 40219589819, corpus commit `bafb7a546` on `main`): of
    21,456 cert-form live-slice rows it read 21,333 and filled 21,183 that
    were NULL, raised none and held none at the latch, leaving 123
    unobservable rows, which the cut buckets as `(unknown)`.

  **What moved, in the predict prompt.** The document list names the two
  cert-stage kinds and *Stage: merits* the United States' merits brief; the
  `argued` moment describes the features file and says a count is never a
  vote; the cert anchoring reads the amicus cut beside the relist and CVSG
  cuts as a marginal stakes proxy; and the vote block is pointed at the
  per-Justice section, pooled only over Terms strictly before the case's
  grant Term.

  **What this label does not release.** The same-question petition list
  (`fedcourts same-question`) stays out of cells: its index is built over the
  whole frame, and staging it per cell needs a plan-job step this label does
  not add. The decision-below input waits on its match-rate measurement. The
  authorship tally (`record/authorship-tally.json`) stays withheld
  (`provision.AUTHORSHIP_TALLY_WITHHELD`).

  **No scored figure moves.** No baseline reads either new statpack section:
  the amicus cut publishes rates no claim is scored against, and the
  per-Justice section is a reference point for the vote block, whose
  `vote_accuracy` would be scored against the outcome's recorded votes, not a
  baseline, and no merits outcome carries recorded votes yet.

- **OT2017 to OT2022's applications are back-filled into the interim docket,
  moving the population the pooled interim base rate is computed over,
  2026-10-26.** A **scoring-baseline** entry, and a **conditioning** one
  through the same number. It registers six Terms' applies before they run:
  the `application-backfill` run-repair pass (`fedcourts
  backfill-applications`), with OT2017, OT2018, OT2019, OT2020, OT2021 and
  OT2022 joining `REGISTERED_APPLY_TERMS` in the same change. Each Term is
  still its own dispatch, its own bound and its own control. No prompt byte,
  registry field or stamp moves, so no digest moves: `uv run fedcourts
  process-digest --all` prints `proc-v13` and the same six blessed digests
  before and after the change.

  **What moves, and why.** The live channel never polled these Terms. The
  corpus holds a CourtListener stub for each of their application numbers,
  with no ask and no disposition, and the statpack counts every one as
  `unparsed`. So they contribute nothing to the substantive pool today,
  although they already sit inside the registered window: an interim cell's
  pool is every Term strictly before its own application Term within
  `salience.base_rate_lookback_terms` (10), so all six are in the window of
  every OT2024, OT2025 and OT2026 cell. **This completes data under the
  existing rule; it is not a rule change.** The window does not move (its
  config comment forbids moving it part-way through a Term), and whether a
  shorter interim window should apply from OT2027 stays the separate
  decision the OT2023 entry deferred. The pass lands each stub through the
  live channel's own ingest seam, so it arrives parsed and joins the pool.
  The provisioned statpack's interim section is what interim cells anchor
  on, and its pooled rate is the baseline their harness skill is stamped
  against, so both move for every interim cell provisioned or stamped after
  the first statpack refresh that follows an apply. The reason to land these
  Terms now rather than after that decision is the executive-action
  emergency-docket replication, which needs every substantive application
  from 2017-01-20 on.

  **When the applies run.** Only after this entry and the registration reach
  `main` in a promotion; only the dry runs ran before it. The pooled figures
  above are a projection from the dry-run ledgers; the applies' own ledgers
  and the next statpack are the record.

  **One break, not six.** The statpack refresh, not the apply, is the break:
  interim cells anchor on and are scored against the committed statpack.
  Each refresh that falls between two applies would be its own anchor move.
  The metrics refresh runs on its weekly cron (Monday 05:41 UTC) and on a
  `run-analytics` `metrics-refresh` dispatch, so the six applies are
  dispatched within one Monday-to-Monday window, with no refresh dispatched
  by hand until the last has landed. If a refresh does fall between two
  applies, each pool it reads is a dated value of its own, named below with
  the refresh that produced it, rather than read as this projection.

  **The straddling cohort, and how interim skill is read.** Interim skill is
  read keyed on the stamped `segment_base_rate` value, never pooled across
  values, as the OT2023 entry registered. At `main` `a0daa0ccf`, 54 interim
  events carry a prediction: 44 have an evaluation and 10 are open. The 10
  open events will be scored against whichever pool stands when they are
  stamped. Nine are OT2026 applications, scored after the refresh against
  ≈0.120 instead of ≈0.093; one is an OT2025 application, scored against
  ≈0.130 instead of ≈0.106. Their cells were provisioned from 2026-08-16 to
  2026-10-23, so they anchored on the pool current at each provisioning run
  (31/296, 53/549 or 51/547 for OT2026 cells), and some events carry
  predictions at two of those anchors. As the OT2023 entry registered, the
  stamp records only the scoring side; the anchoring side is read from each
  cell's provisioning run id against the refresh commits' times. For scale:
  a forecast of 0.10 on a denial has Brier skill **−0.15** against 51/547 =
  0.0932 and **+0.30** against 151/1259 = 0.1199. Under the
  pooled reading declared on 2026-10-11, the refresh is a dated,
  digest-silent boundary, so a pooled interim figure carries its `n` on each
  side of it.

- **The contact scrub reads a mailing block whose street type is abbreviated,
  and withholds the city line below a street; recorded 2026-10-28.** A
  **conditioning** entry in the *what the pipeline provisions* class, under
  unchanged digests: no prompt byte and no registry field the digests read
  moves, and `uv run fedcourts process-digest --all` at this commit prints
  what it prints at its parent on `staging`: `proc-v13` and the six digests
  `6a176c28…` (claude-baseline), `2827480e…` (codex-baseline), `b69b2b3a…`
  (gemini-baseline), `167b7d71…` (claude-judge), `a8610eec…` (codex-judge)
  and `6a88d3dc…` (gemini-judge).

  **What changes**, on the staged copy alone
  (`pipeline.documents.scrub_contact_details` and the residual detector).
  - **The value pass reads a street type in either spelling.** An address
    value's street-type or unit word (`Drive`/`Dr`, `Street`/`St`,
    `Avenue`/`Ave`, `Court`/`Ct`, `Place`/`Pl`, `Apartment`/`Apt` and the rest
    of `_STREET_TYPE_SPELLINGS`)
    matches any of its spellings, so a docket `Address` of "… Drive" withholds
    a cover line that prints "… Dr". Only the docket's own value widens.
  - **The shape pass reads `Dr`, `Ct` and `Pl` as the first line of a mailing
    block.** A street line ending on one of them is withheld where a "City,
    State ZIP" line sits directly below it. On their own the three stay
    unread, as before, since they are a doctor, the court and a plaintiff far
    more often than a street.
  - **The city line below a withheld street address or box is withheld**
    where the shape pass runs (the docket's own address value counts as a
    withheld street), as a placeholder of its own, so the block keeps its line
    count and each line its placeholder. A "City, State ZIP" line under
    anything else stays, which is the shape the Court's own address line takes
    with no street line above it; one under a court or clerk street address is
    withheld with it.
  - **The residual detector counts a `Dr`, `Ct` or `Pl` street line with a
    city line directly below it** on the opening and closing, so a block the
    scrub still misses (a street name in lower case) reads
    `contact_scrubbed: false`.

  flagged (`evt-petition-arrival-disposition`), provisioned from the

  **A harness boundary under the 2026-10-11 pooled rule.** The change moves
  what a predict cell reads under unchanged digests, so it is composition and

  - **Exposure is an upper bound and is not sized.** Which self-represented
    dockets print a mailing block with an abbreviated street type, or a city

  **What changes.** `pipeline.outcome.persist_moment_events`, the one write

  row's. The corpus event's title still re-tracks the row on every re-mint.
  A moment mint re-fires on every poll that still sees its trigger (the
  CVSG, SG brief, call-for-response, relist, interim response and later merits
  moments), so from this entry's carrying merge a minted moment's committed
  file keeps the caption the moment was first minted under, which is the caption a prediction on it was made under,
  and the check reads it as it reads a baseline's. A committed file the check
  could not read as a witness is rewritten whole, as before. Every other field
  is still written from the post-upsert corpus row.

  and no committed file is rewritten by it. Every committed minted-moment
  definition at the parent (among them 91 call-for-response, 21 response
  requested, 19 relist, 17 CVSG, 4 SG brief, and 52, 22 and 6 order, brief
  and argument merits definitions, by directory count) keeps what it carries

  **What the rule still misses.** A re-docketing that falls before a moment's
  first mint is invisible to its definition, as for a baseline before its

  same petition (a substituted party) is kept at its first-mint rendering in
