- **Gemini rows carry the call's logged outcome, and codex logs gain the
  cell's subagent sessions, 2026-10-28.** Two **capture** changes of the
  masking-surface class, in one PR. No digest, constant, window, boundary or
  membership rule moves, and `uv run fedcourts process-digest --all` prints the
  same `proc-v13` digests at the change as at its base.

  **Gemini.** Gemini CLI 0.49's `gemini_cli.tool_call` record carries the
  call's `success` bit, a failed call's message, and, with prompt logging on
  as the cell workflows set it, a shell command's non-zero exit in `metadata`.
  Capture now reads them. Every gemini row is `result_capture` `outcome_only`
  where it was `unobserved`, with `result_status` `error` where the CLI marked
  the call failed (its `success` false, an error message logged, or a shell
  command's non-zero exit), `throttled` where a manifest call's failure message
  carries the 429 shape (read after the CLI's `with response:` wrapper where it
  quotes the call's own arguments, else the whole message), and `ok` otherwise. Digests and
  document dates stay null, because the payload is still not logged.
  - **What it reaches through the blinded log.** The mask passes both markers
    through, so every evaluator now sees, on a gemini candidate, which calls
    the engine marked failed. That is the point: a judge reading a
    `fedcourts query` row against a `retrieval.md` that reports no retrieval
    can tell a failed attempt from an undisclosed one. The evaluate prompt
    describes `captured` and `unobserved` only; it is not edited here, so an
    `outcome_only` row reaches a judge described by its own name and the
    field's schema description until a re-bless adds a line for it. A judge
    applying the prompt literally may read an `outcome_only` row's null digest
    as "returned nothing", so blinded leakage grades of gemini candidates sit
    on a capture seam across the merge. An all-`outcome_only` log identifies
    the gemini candidate as surely as an all-`unobserved` one did.
  - **What it moves on published surfaces.** Gemini manifest calls enter the
    throttle denominator for the first time: the log's `throttled_calls`, the
    run PR's throttle note, and the tool-usage report's per-engine throttle
    cut. Gemini's figure sees a 429 the server raised as a tool error and never
    the citation tools' note on a successful result, so it is a narrower floor
    than claude's or codex's. Gemini logs captured before the carrying merge
    stay `unobserved` and add nothing to it, so a gemini throttle figure is
    scoped to logs captured after the merge, and a move across it is a capture
    change. `result_capture_coverage` does not move: it counts `captured` rows
    only.

  **Codex.** Capture read the newest `rollout-*.jsonl` under the cell's
  sessions directory, and a subagent session started after the parent's last
  write is the newest file. It now reads the parent session (the newest
  rollout whose `session_meta` names no parent thread and no subagent source),
  every subagent session descending from it, and any subagent session in the
  cell's directory that names no parent: calls merge in timestamp order, and
  token counts sum. A subagent forked with its parent's history copies the
  parent's token events and continues its running total, so only what it adds
  past the inherited total counts; the fork copies no tool call, so no row
  repeats. A tree with no top-level `session_meta` reads the newest rollout
  alone.
  - **What it reaches.** A codex candidate's staged log can gain rows a
    subagent made, which is retrieval the cell did and which the judge
    previously could not see. A codex cell's `usage.json` tokens and estimated
    cost rise by the subagent's use, so measured spend moves with them, under
    the same process version: a codex $/cell measured across the carrying
    merge pools two capture regimes that no digest separates, and earlier
    codex measurements leave subagent spend out, so a re-anchor of codex's
    planning rate reads cells after the merge only. Subagent tokens are priced
    at the parent's requested model, and `served_models` reads the parent
    session alone, so a subagent on another model is priced as the parent.
  - **What it does not repair.** The 10 of 675 committed codex logs (counted
    2026-10-16) that looked like a subagent's session keep what they carry,
    and so do the same cells' `usage.json`, which count the subagent's tokens
    rather than the parent's: capture runs once, and those rollouts are gone.

  The parsers were built against the Gemini CLI 0.49 and Codex 0.144.1 sources
  and exercised on fixtures shaped from them; no real engine log was read for
  this entry, so both readings are unverified until the first round after the
  carrying merge. The runnable effect check once it is live, on the first
  predict round after the carrying merge: across its gemini
  `retrieval_log.json` files, `jq '[.calls[].result_status] | unique'` prints
  more than `["ok"]` on at least one cell (a status read from a real
  `success` or error field, not the residual), and across its `usage.json`
  files `jq .served_models` is non-null on each engine's cells; on the first
  evaluate round, each cell directory carries a `blinding.json`; and `uv run
  fedcourts process-digest --all` prints the same label and six digests at
  the carrying merge as at its first parent.

  Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-29` (merge commit `116bd569e4d44e5d9ff2878bce34b4b903f206ba`, merged `2026-10-29T14:16:26Z`).

- **A merits event on a proceeding that ended with nothing decided closes
  without an outcome, `merits-terminated`; recorded 2026-10-28.** A
  **membership** entry: it states the terminal state of a forecast that can
  never be graded, and moves no scored figure. It moves no digest: no prompt
  template, neither agent config and not `src/fedcourtsai/process_version.py`
  changes, and `uv run fedcourts process-digest --all` at this commit prints
  `proc-v13` and the six digests the entries above list.

  **What changes.** `pipeline.judgment.backfill_merits_judgments`, the
  run-seed step that stamps `merits_terminated`, now also closes every open
  merits-stage event on a row whose termination says the proceeding ended
  with nothing decided (a Rule 46 dismissal, a dismissal as moot, an
  abatement, a grant the Court vacated). Each is marked
  `resolved_without_outcome` with the new reason `merits-terminated`. No
  outcome is written, and the termination is never read as an undisturbed
  judgment. A row whose only terminal entry is the bare mandate notation
  (`judgment-issued`) is a decided docket the parser missed, and its events
  stay open. The outcome passes leave a `merits-terminated` event alone while
  its row stays terminated; if a judgment later parses, the parse clears the
  termination and the convergence records the outcome over the mark.

  **What a closed event owes.** Nothing. The evaluate backlog
  (`pipeline.pull.derive_evaluate_backlog`) and `store.resolved_events` leave
  out a `merits-terminated` event: with no `outcome.json` there is no ground
  truth to grade, and a cell minted on one could only fail at model cost. The missed-forecast scan leaves out a
  `merits-terminated` event, which was never decided: it is neither a missed
  forecast nor a missing outcome record.

  **What moves**, read 2026-10-28 from the production corpus under
  `origin/main`'s pointer (`5e42eb35…`, latest pull 2026-10-28) and the
  ledger at `origin/main`. Twelve open merits events on nine dockets carry a
  termination other than the mandate notation: 19-825 (`grant-vacated`) and
  20-429, 20-454, 20-539, 20-794, 20-1374, 20-1541, 24-413 and 25-886
  (`voluntary-dismissal`). Only 25-886 (`scotus/73280386`,
  `evt-order-judgment`) carries committed predictions: three forward cells
  of run `20260816T111104Z`, one per predictor. They were never graded and
  now never will be, and no evaluate cell is minted on them. The other cells
  on these events are failed attempts.
  **0 scored outcomes move**, and no base rate re-prices: a terminated row
  was already outside the merits pool's `parsed` slice.

  The runnable effect check once it is live: run-seed's merits backfill step
  (its daily scheduled window, or a dispatch) prints `closed 12 open merits
  event(s) without an outcome` on its first run after the carrying promotion
  and `closed 0` after; `uv run fedcourts backfill-merits-judgments` (a dry
  run, where the corpus is pulled) prints `would close 12` before it; and `uv
  run pytest tests/test_judgment.py tests/test_outcome.py
  tests/test_evaluate_backlog.py tests/test_missed_forecasts.py -k
  "terminat or without_an_outcome"` is green.

- **`proc-v14`: the predict and evaluate prompts take the flag vocabulary,
  the harness clock and the call-for-response moment; recorded 2026-10-28.**
  Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-29` (merge `116bd569e4d44e5d9ff2878bce34b4b903f206ba`,
  `2026-10-29T14:16:26Z`), to be tagged **`prereg/proc-v14`**. Registered under
  the merge-stamped rule, so its counting instant, its six bless moments and
  every window edge it moves are the carrying merge's committer time. It is
  the first label to move all six digests at once, so it takes two
  supersession shapes together
  ([process-version.md](process-version.md#freezing-the-cutover-procedure)):
  `.github/prompts/predict.md` changes, so each predictor's open `proc-v13`
  window **closes** at this label's instant and a `proc-v14` window opens
  there for each new digest (the third shape); and
  `.github/prompts/evaluate.md` changes, so the three judges' blessings are
  replaced (the second shape). Nothing is de-counted and nothing is re-owed:
  every cell counted in a closed window keeps counting under its own label.
  Until the carrying merge stamps the six new blessings, the carried bless map
  is empty while `FROZEN_SINCE` stays at `proc-v13`'s instant; every board
  built in that interval counts nothing of this label, the safe direction.

  **What moved, in the predict prompt.**
  - *Sources.* The CourtListener tools are for lower-court records; the
    docket's own state comes from the snapshot and the Court's site. A
    forward cell that meets a claimed outcome of its own case checks it
    against the docket and, where it cannot, flags it unverified.
  - *The replay boundary* is stated as the context's `cutoff`, with the
    docket's decided-before Term named as the coarser bound it is; a replay
    cell's disclosure of outcome-revealing material is written under the
    `leakage-disclosure` category.
  - *Flags.* The prompt lists the category vocabulary (`provisioning`,
    `capture-gap`, `leakage-disclosure` among them), defines each severity,
    offers the optional `issue` field, and tells the cell never to write
    `source` or `normalised`. `blocked` is no longer offered; a cell that
    could not finish writes the category that names why, at severity
    `blocker`. The "good hygiene" note is dropped: a decisive signal belongs
    in `reasoning.md`.
  - *Corpus commands* are spelled `uv run fedcourts query` and `uv run
    fedcourts open-events`, with a note on `PATH`, `--help`, and at least one
    filtered query.
  - *The distribution moment* is placed at no cut (`cutoff: null`), so its
    snapshot is the docket as last stored, and the prompt says so.
  - *The vote block* is scored only against a complete record over the whole
    bench.
  - *`created_at`* may be any timestamp: the stamp overwrites it.
  - *`retrieval.md`* lists every call the cell attempted, a failed or refused
    one included, since the harness log records them all.
  - *Paper-only filings* in the context are named.
  - *`prediction_summary.md`*: every predict cell writes a plain-language
    summary of about 80 words beside its other files (the stamp warns past
    160). It is display material, read by no scorer and staged to no judge
    (the blinded staging copies only allowlisted files); the stamp warns on a
    missing or overlong one and refuses nothing.
  - *The cert call-for-response moment* (`moment: response-requested`, event
    `evt-order-call-for-response-disposition`) is named, so a cell placed on
    it knows what it is.

  **What moved, in the evaluate prompt.** The same `created_at`, corpus
  command, flag vocabulary and `cutoff: null` lines; what an `outcome_only`
  retrieval-log row means (a call whose ending the log carried but not its
  result); the `vote_accuracy`
  completeness rule in both places it is described; and the claim-set names,
  which now read `interim-v2` and `merits-v2`. That pays the amendment debt
  the `proc-v12` entry left for the next label to move the judges.

  **What the harness releases with this label.**
  - *The cert call-for-response moment is forecastable.* It was declared,
    parsed and minted (92 committed definitions at `origin/main` `a0a526439`) but filed no
    cell. A cell on it is admitted only until a conference the petition was
    distributed for on or after the call has sat
    (`store._CONFERENCE_BOUNDED_MOMENTS`, the bound the relist and sg-brief
    moments already carry), so the events minted for petitions called on long
    before the switch-on should never be filed: a conference has already sat
    on them. That is read from the code and the store tests, not from a
    dry-run over the corpus; the `predict-plan` effect check below settles
    it. The moment is not in `REPREDICT_MOMENTS`. It is scored separately
    and never pooled with another cert moment. No committed table conditions
    on a called-for response, so the prompt anchors the cell on its band and
    asks it to say how far the call moves it.
  - *`relist-increment` is masked as vacuous on that moment*
    (`pipeline.claims._MOMENT_VACUOUS`): a petition the Court called for a
    response on is distributed again once the response is in or its time
    runs out, so the count is all but certain to rise. The claim has no
    baseline today and scores nowhere, so the mask moves no scored figure;
    it keeps a resolved `1` from standing beside a certain forecast once a
    baseline lands.
  - *A consolidated member's briefed moment* opens on the lead docket's
    merits brief where the member's own row records none
    (`merits_brief_on_lead`). The member latch is written after ingest, so
    the moment mints one poll after the lead's brief.
  - *The flag roll-up* names the untracked issue a row cites.

  **What scored figures move.** None in the headline: no baseline, rate or
  membership rule moves, and the call-for-response cells are a new
  population with no prior cell to compare against, whose own block's skill
  is not claimable until a floor conditioned on the call is registered
  ([metrics/README.md](../metrics/README.md)). Headline *membership* can
  still move through the judges: the leakage exclusion drops a grading with
  `leakage_suspected` from every scored figure, the ranked
  `cert@distribution` arm included, and the evaluate prompt now reads a
  distribution cell's later docket entries as provisioned input (the
  evaluator half below). At `a0a526439`, 23 committed gradings carry
  `leakage_suspected: true`, 18 of them on `evt-petition-disposition`, so an
  exclusion count on that arm reads per rubric. One diagnostic moves in
  definition: the back-tests' `outcome_exposure_candidate` bit is set on any
  flag written under `leakage-disclosure` as well as on the message
  heuristic, so a candidate count read across this boundary, the cert
  back-test's and the merits back-test's `exposure_candidates` alike,
  compares two rules ([metrics/README.md](../metrics/README.md)).

  **The retiring evaluator digests, and what was graded under them.**
  `sha256:167b7d71…` (`claude-judge`), `sha256:a8610eec…` (`codex-judge`) and
  `sha256:6a88d3dc…` (`gemini-judge`) leave the blessed set. At `origin/main`
  `a0a526439` they stamp **174**, **87** and **87** committed evaluations, and
  `store.stratify` over that ledger keeps **156**, **84** and **84** of them
  in scope, **324** counted cells in all. Each keeps counting on its timing
  (`graded_in_window`); only the constant stops naming the digest, so this
  entry is where the grading process behind them stays recorded. Because an
  evaluator digest records and never partitions, every judge's grading series
  pools across this rubric boundary, and a judge-dependent figure that spans
  it reads per rubric ([metrics/README.md](../metrics/README.md)). Two
  grading criteria moved with the rubric text. The judge reads a
  distribution cell's later docket entries as provisioned input, not
  retrieval, so a leakage call on such a cell can differ across the boundary;
  `leakage_suspected` series on distribution cells read per rubric. And
  `vote_accuracy` is written only against a complete vote record, which no
  committed merits outcome carries yet, so no grade moves on it today.

- **A cell's context records what the snapshot contact scrub withheld;
  recorded 2026-10-29.** A record change with no reading rule and no scored
  figure.

  **Why.** On a docket read as self-represented, provisioning stages the
  snapshot with that filer's contact keys replaced by placeholders. The only
  record of it was the placeholders themselves and the run log's counts, and
  the log expires. A staged snapshot with no placeholder therefore read the
  same whether the scrub ran and found nothing or never ran. The document
  scrub already says this per file in `documents.json`; the snapshot scrub
  said nothing.

  **The record.** `PredictionContext` gains `snapshot_contact_scrub`:
  - `sides`, the counsel-block lists the docket was read as self-represented
    on, which is the scrub's trigger; empty where it did not run;
  - `blocks` and `fields`, the blocks that had a value withheld and the
    values withheld, both zero where `sides` is empty.

  It is written on every cell `write_cell_record` provisions, forward and
  replay alike. It is null on the cert back-test's replay contexts, whose
  provisioner redacts the snapshot by its own rule and runs no contact scrub,
  and on every cell provisioned before the carrying merge. The cell reads
  `record/context.json`, so the field joins its information set. It adds
  nothing the cell could not already see, since the placeholders are in the
  staged snapshot, and it carries counts only, never a withheld value. No
  prompt text or other digest input changes, so no digest moves. The summary
  prompt, which is outside every digest, gains a line telling the summary
  writer the placeholders are the pipeline's and not to be repeated.
  - **The registry row.** The boundary is `context-snapshot-contact-scrub`.
    It applies to every predictor, with reach `all`, and is not gradual:
    every cell provisioned after the carrying merge carries the record. It is
    registered **pending** in this change's own PR
    (`fedcourts register-boundary`). Its `merge` and `at` stay null until the
    promotion merge that carries it to `main` stamps them
    (`promotion-record`).
  - **Expected population.** Every newly provisioned cell carries the record.
    A non-empty `sides` appears exactly where the run log's existing
    snapshot-scrub line appears, so the record changes no cell's staged
    snapshot or documents. No corpus count was taken for this entry.

  **What it moves.** No scored figure. Once cells sit on both sides of the
  stamped boundary, each pooled entry's and each paired engine's `boundaries`
  list gains a `context-snapshot-contact-scrub` row. That row is composition,
  not a cut. The field is no cut, exclusion or rank key on any board. A later
  dated entry must register one before any figure reads it.

  Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-29` (merge commit `116bd569e4d44e5d9ff2878bce34b4b903f206ba`, merged `2026-10-29T14:16:26Z`).

  The runnable effect check once it is live:
  - `uv run pytest tests/test_snapshot_scrub.py -k scrub_record` and `uv run
    pytest tests/test_cli_provision.py -k snapshot_scrub_ran` are green;
  - on the first predict run's collect PR after the carrying merge, `jq -c
    '.context.snapshot_contact_scrub'
    data/cases/scotus/*/events/*/predictions/*/<run_id>/prediction.json`
    prints an object, never `null`, for every file;
  - on `main`, `uv run python -c
    "from fedcourtsai.process_version import HARNESS_BOUNDARIES as H;
    print('context-snapshot-contact-scrub' in {b.name for b in H})"` prints
    `True` once the promotion record has stamped the row.

- **A bare `fedcourts` resolves in every agent's shell, and each cell's
  retrieval log counts the requests its corpus sidecar answered; recorded
  2026-10-29.** An environment change with no reading rule and no scored
  figure, and a harness record beside it.

  **Why.** The agent shell had `uv` but not the project's own `fedcourts` on
  its PATH, so a cell that ran `fedcourts query` without the `uv run` prefix
  got "command not found" and either retried or dropped the corpus. Cells of
  every engine did both, gemini's most often, in the predict run diagnosed on
  2026-09-28 (23 gemini cells compared against their sidecar logs). The
  prompts now spell `uv run fedcourts`; this makes the bare form work too.
  Separately, whether a cell's query reached the corpus service could only be
  read from the engine's transcript and the cell's own report, which differ by
  engine in what they show.

  **The environment half.** The predict and evaluate cell jobs symlink the
  project venv's `fedcourts` into `/usr/local/bin` after the venv is built.
  It is the same binary `uv run fedcourts` runs, so a command that worked
  before gives the same answer; what changes is that the bare spelling now
  runs instead of failing. `/usr/local/bin` is on codex's `secure_path`, so
  codex's separate account reaches it too. No prompt text or other digest
  input changes, so no digest moves.
  - **The registry row.** The boundary is `agent-shell-fedcourts-on-path`. It
    applies to every predictor, with reach `all`, and is not gradual: every
    cell run after the carrying merge has the bare command. It is registered
    **pending** in this change's own PR (`fedcourts register-boundary`). Its
    `merge` and `at` stay null until the promotion merge that carries it to
    `main` stamps them (`promotion-record`).
  - **Expected population.** Every cell after the carrying merge. Only a cell
    that types the bare command is affected, and its transcript shows it.

  **The record half.** `retrieval_log.json` gains `corpus_service`, the
  `/v1/query` and `/v1/open-events` requests the cell's corpus sidecar logged
  and how many it answered 200, counted by the capture step off the sidecar's
  request log. The collect job's prior-availability note gains a line naming,
  per actor, the cells whose sidecar logged no query. It changes nothing a
  cell reads, and the blinding mask drops it, so it reaches no grader. It
  needs no boundary.

  **What it moves.** No scored figure. Once cells sit on both sides of the
  stamped boundary, each pooled entry's and each paired engine's `boundaries`
  list gains an `agent-shell-fedcourts-on-path` row. That row is composition,
  not a cut. Neither the boundary nor `corpus_service` is a cut, exclusion or
  rank key on any board. A later dated entry must register one before any
  figure reads either.

  Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-29` (merge commit `116bd569e4d44e5d9ff2878bce34b4b903f206ba`, merged `2026-10-29T14:16:26Z`).

  The runnable effect check once it is live:
  - on the first predict run after the carrying merge, a cell job's log shows
    the "Put the project CLI on the agent shell's PATH" step green, and `jq -c
    '.corpus_service'
    data/cases/scotus/*/events/*/predictions/*/<run_id>/retrieval_log.json`
    prints an object, never `null`, for every file;
  - the run PR's body carries the sidecar line only where some cell's sidecar
    logged no query, naming that actor's count against its own cells;
  - on `main`, `uv run python -c
    "from fedcourtsai.process_version import HARNESS_BOUNDARIES as H;
    print('agent-shell-fedcourts-on-path' in {b.name for b in H})"` prints

- **The live-duplicate dedupe merges a pair that a caption-only CourtListener
  row sits beside, and nine cert-stage dispositions stop counting twice;
  recorded 2026-10-29.** A corpus convergence under an unchanged digest that
  moves published statpack counts.

  **Why.** `dedupe-live-rows` merges a SCOTUS number held under both a
  CourtListener docket id and a live-minted reserved-range id, but it took only
  exact two-row groups. Nine numbers carry a third CourtListener row that
  asserts no disposition, filing, decision, cert or live-poll date: `17-1107`,
  `17-9572`, `18-1109`, `19-1302`, `20-1009`, `20-1084`, `21-439`, `21-511`
  and `21-846`. Read ranged from the blob at `main` `d8b560718` (latest pull
  2026-10-28, latest snapshot 2026-07-13), the CourtListener row and the live
  twin agree on filing date, cert-grant date and disposition for all nine
  (eight `granted`, one `gvr`), both rows carry `last_live_polled`, and for
  the eight grants both carry the same `merits_judgment` and
  `merits_decided`. So each of the nine is two rows in every figure that
  counts rows. The 2026-10-18 entry above named eight of them as this
  pattern; `17-9572` is the ninth.

  **The change.** The candidate rule sets aside any CourtListener row
  asserting none of `disposition`, `date_filed`, `date_decided`,
  `date_cert_granted`, `date_cert_denied` or `last_live_polled` before
  counting the group, provided every such row's docket id sits above the
  survivor's. In all nine groups the caption-only row's id is the highest.
  The merge then runs as for any pair, and the caption-only row stays in
  place, untouched. It runs in run-seed's dedupe step, which runs in the daily
  02:31 UTC window, so the nine converge in the first such window after the
  carrying promotion with no dispatch.

  **What it moves.** Every row-counting statpack figure that reads these rows
  loses one row per number:
  - the pack-level `corpus_rows` and the court and era sections, by nine;
  - the live-slice totals and the live-slice cert-stage sections (the relist,
    CVSG and amicus cuts among them);
  - the per-Term cert-stage figures for OT2017 to OT2021: eight grants and one
    GVR, in the paid or IFP class each serial falls in;
  - the merits section, from the Term of each grant: `granted`, `parsed` and
    the judgment counts lose the eight grants: two `affirmed` (`17-1107`,
    `18-1109`), five `reversed` (`17-9572`, `20-1009`, `20-1084`, `21-439`,
    `21-511`) and one `vacated` (`21-846`). The GVR enters no merits row.

  No committed prediction, evaluation or graded figure sits under a dropped
  live id. Eight keep a baseline `event.yaml` and `outcome.json` under the
  dropped id, by the dedupe's design, and one carries nothing; no rate or
  census reads them. Baselines pooled from a statpack refreshed after the
  merge read the deduplicated counts: the cert band rates and the merits
  disturbed rate, whose ten-Term windows cover OT2017 to OT2021, so a stamp,
  re-grade or merits grading after that refresh draws on them.

  **The boundary.** An OT2017 to OT2021 per-Term cert-stage or merits figure,
  or a baseline pooled over those Terms, from a statpack refreshed before the
  carrying merge is not compared or pooled with one refreshed after it.

  Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-29` (merge commit `116bd569e4d44e5d9ff2878bce34b4b903f206ba`, merged `2026-10-29T14:16:26Z`).

  The runnable effect check once it is live: the first 02:31 UTC run-seed
  window after the carrying merge drops the nine live ids in its "Dedupe
  live-minted duplicate rows" step, and
  `uv run fedcourts dedupe-live-rows` on a freshly pulled corpus then prints
  `would drop 0 live-minted row(s)`.

- **The live rotation keeps ten slots a cycle for never-polled rows, oldest
  Term first; recorded 2026-10-29.** A **membership-rule** entry under
  unchanged digests: no digest or `salience_version` moves, but which rows the
  live channel refreshes, and so which rows carry live facts and, rarely,
  which petitions selection sees, can.

  **What moved.** `live_rotation` takes `live.never_polled_reserve_per_run`
  (10 in `config/tracking.yaml`) slots of each cycle's `live.max_cases_per_run`
  for rows the channel has never polled: a SCOTUS Term-prefixed cert number
  (no applications) at or above the rotation's Term floor, undecided, with no
  disposition and an open event, no row under the same number already polled,
  and the row the identity join resolves the number to. They are ordered
  oldest Term first. The reserve takes only what the overdue and distributed
  rows leave, so neither moves and the reserve yields while an overdue backlog
  drains; it displaces the tail of the Term tiers, which the staleness bound
  keeps from going stale. At twelve cycles a day that reaches up to about 120
  rows a day.

  **Why it is a boundary.** The Term tiers lead with the newest Terms, which
  fill the cap on their own, so a past-Term row the historical walker skipped
  (undecided when walked, or never served) was never polled. Polling it writes
  what a live poll writes (disposition, dates, counsel, the snapshot and
  `last_live_polled`), so the row enters the live slice and every row-counting
  statpack figure that reads the live slice or a disposition. Its weight is
  `legacy_denial_sample_weight`'s, as for any live poll: 1 on a block the
  walker has enumerated. Read ranged from the blob at `main` `d8b560718`
  (latest pull 2026-10-28, latest snapshot 2026-07-13), the reserve's backlog
  is about 20,800 rows: OT2017 47, OT2018 4,238, OT2019 3,403, OT2020 3,013,
  OT2021 2,867, OT2022 2,530, OT2023 2,480 and OT2024 2,210, counted before
  the identity join, which can only lower them; the reserve's first 120
  picks are OT2017's 47 and 73 from OT2018. At up to 120 rows a day the
  reserve alone would take months to drain it. The historical-ifp re-walks in flight for OT2018 to OT2025 re-open the
  IFP stream only, so the reserve is the sole route to OT2017's rows and to
  every paid-stream row. A reserved row that is in fact still pending can gain
  a distribution and enter the selection pool as any polled row would.

  The reached rows are not a random slice of their Terms. Most were undecided
  when the walker read them, which selects slow resolvers (holds, CVSGs,
  relists); the likely direction is a grant rate above their Term's, which
  would make the pre-boundary per-Term rates the biased ones, but nothing here
  measures it in advance, and the counts above are rows, not an effect size.

  **The boundary** is a drift, not a step: the reserve adds rows in every
  cycle with free slots until its backlog drains, so two statpacks refreshed
  after the carrying merge also differ. It starts at the first scheduled live
  window after that merge and ends when the check below reports a zero
  backlog. A per-Term cert-stage or live-slice figure for OT2017 onward, or a
  baseline pooled over those Terms (the cert band rates), from a statpack
  refreshed inside that window or before it is not compared or pooled with one
  refreshed after it; a prediction stamped after such a refresh draws on the
  moved baseline.

  Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-29-2` (merge commit `7dde3572fb8db291cf4e8c8d992b517e42a2a28a`, merged `2026-10-29T22:36:30Z`).

  The runnable effect check once it is live: after a day of live windows
  with reserve slots free, `CHECK_SUMMARY=out.md uv run python
  scripts/checks/never_polled_reserve.py` over a freshly pulled corpus shows
  the OT2017 row gone from its table, or holding only rows whose poll failed
  in transit, which the live cycle's failed queue names; its total falls with
  each later run until it reaches zero.

  The run reads the ledger and registry at `origin/main`'s `1b197495a`
  (`2026-10-29T16:08:11Z`), after the stamp and after the first `proc-v14`

    closed proc-v13 claude-baseline: 7 counted event(s) — 0 resolved, 7 pending at close
    closed proc-v13 gemini-baseline: 7 counted event(s) — 0 resolved, 7 pending at close

    codex-baseline: 24 successor-counted event(s); earlier window proc-v13: 0 failed, 0 uncounted cell, 0 missing, 24 not reached before the close
    gemini-baseline: 23 successor-counted event(s); earlier window proc-v13: 0 failed, 0 uncounted cell, 0 missing, 23 not reached before the close

- **The never-polled reserve takes its slots while the distributed petitions
  fill the cycle; recorded 2026-10-30.** A **membership-rule** entry under
  unchanged digests, amending the 2026-10-29 reserve entry.

  **What moved.** That entry's reserve yielded to the distributed tier as
  well as the overdue one. Through the Term the distributed petitions alone
  hold more than `live.max_cases_per_run`: on the blob at `main` `e4e50ee4a`
  (the live window's pointer, 2026-10-30 09:36 UTC), 290 pending petitions
  were distributed for the 2026-11-06 conference and 27 for 2026-11-13,
  against a cap of 150. On the same blob no OT2017 or OT2018 row carries a
  live poll dated 2026-10-30, so the five live windows of that day before it,
  all after the carrying merge of 2026-10-29 22:36 UTC, reached no
  never-polled row of either Term. It now yields only to the overdue tier
  (the first `live.max_overdue_per_run` stale rows) and otherwise displaces
  the cycle's tail, its rows listed last. In Term that tail is the most
  recently polled petitions of the last conference the cycle reaches. It is
  capped at half of `live.max_cases_per_run`.

  **Why it is a boundary.** Ten slots move from distributed petitions to
  never-polled rows, a fifteenth of the cap with the overdue tier empty and a
  tenth of what is left with it full. While a conference's set exceeds the
  cap its petitions' re-polls stretch by 15/14 to 10/9, so a distribution
  transition, which fires predict, is read that much later at most. While a
  past conference's set still awaiting its order-list read exceeds the cap,
  that conference is the tail: up to ten of its petitions a cycle read the
  order list one cycle later, and within a conference those are the most
  recently polled, the likeliest to have read it already. The 2026-10-29 entry's boundary, a drift until the
  reserve's backlog drains, now starts at this entry's carrying merge rather
  than that entry's, since before it the reserve polled nothing in Term.

  Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-30` (merge commit `a3b2daec8ba19b6c3b3aecb9316bd62c15d568df`, merged `2026-10-30T16:38:43Z`).

  `CHECK_SUMMARY=out.md uv run python scripts/checks/never_polled_reserve.py`
  over a freshly pulled corpus shows the OT2017 row gone from its table, or
  holding only rows whose poll failed in transit; its total falls with each
  later run until it reaches zero.

- **An interim reserve slot frees when its occupant was filed more than 180
  days before the selection pass; recorded 2026-10-29.** A
  **membership-rule** entry under unchanged digests: no value, digest or
  `salience_version` moves, but which pending applications the interim
  reserve funds can. The reserve is applied by `pipeline.salience.plan_cohorts`
  under every scorer, so it is not part of what a salience version names.

  **What moved.** A latched, still-unresolved application held its reserve slot
  until the resolver recorded a disposition or its newest stored snapshot read
  as an interim disposal (the 2026-10-19 entry). From the carrying merge, an
  occupant whose `date_filed` is more than `salience.interim_reserve_age_out_days`
  (180 in `config/tracking.yaml`) days before the selection pass's own date
  also keeps its latch but stops counting against
  `salience.interim_reserve_slots`, and a pending application past the same
  horizon does not contend for a slot, so a freed slot never goes to an
  application the next pass would free again. The age is measured to the
  pass's date (the live cycle's `today`, or `reconcile-salience-selection
  --today`, default today UTC), never the wall clock inside the planner. A
  row with no filing date never ages out. The gate replay passes no date and
  projects no applications, so it ages nothing out.
  `reconcile-salience-selection` now prints each occupant's age at the pass's
  date and, for a released one, whether it aged out or its snapshot reads
  disposed. An aged occupant stays latched and unresolved, so every live
  cycle reads its snapshot again until a pull records the disposition, as for
  a snapshot release.

  **Why it is a boundary.** A freed slot goes to the next application on the
  escalation ladder, and the slots in use lower the current conference's cert
  rank fill one-for-one, so the change can move which applications and which
  cert petitions are selected from the carrying merge on. It moves no cell
  already minted and re-derives nothing committed.

  **The horizon and its evidence.** Read from the production corpus (newest
  pull 2026-10-29), 1,097 substantive applications are decided. Days from
  filing to decision: median 5, 95th percentile 69, 99th percentile 167; 11
  (1%) took more than 180. The figures count decided applications only, so
  they are right-censored: an application still pending today is in none of
  them, and the true share still pending at 180 days is understated.

  **The de-funding risk.** About 1% of decided substantive applications were
  still pending at 180 days, a lower bound for the reason above. An application like them loses its slot before
  it resolves, and a pending application past the horizon is never picked,
  so the funded interim slice under-represents the slowest applications. A
  forward cell already minted for an aged occupant stands; the slot it frees
  funds another application's.

  **What it frees today.** Two slots. A dry run of the selection planner at
  2026-10-29, read ranged against the index pointer `251805e6650ab3cb…` (the
  pointer at `main` `54a2b8d40`), finds five latched, pending occupants, and
  all five hold a slot before the change. 21A85 (`scotus/60667676`, filed
  2021-10-18, 1,837 days, latched substantive and in scope) is one of them and
  is freed; so is the stuck occupant 25A622 (`scotus/73279700`, 338 days).
  26A163 (85 days), 26A458 (23) and 26A560 (8) keep their slots.

  Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-30` (merge commit `a3b2daec8ba19b6c3b3aecb9316bd62c15d568df`, merged `2026-10-30T16:38:43Z`).

  The runnable effect check once it is live: where the corpus is pulled,
  `uv run fedcourts reconcile-salience-selection` (a dry run) prints an
  `interim reserve as of <date>:` line counting the occupants aged out, and
  the 21A85 and 25A622 occupant lines read `released: aged out past 180
  day(s)` while the 26A163 line reads `holds a slot`, for as long as none of
  them has resolved and 26A163 is inside the horizon.

- **`proc-v15`: a cell's prompt template is its whole contract, the cert
  skill anchor is frozen at placement, forward cert cells read their
  same-question list, and run-time installs are refused; recorded
  2026-10-30.** Carried to `main` by `promotion/2026-10-30` (merge
  `a3b2daec8ba19b6c3b3aecb9316bd62c15d568df`, `2026-10-30T16:38:43Z`), to be tagged
  **`prereg/proc-v15`**. Registered under the merge-stamped rule, so its
  counting instant, its six bless moments and every window edge it moves are
  the carrying merge's committer time. Both prompts change, so it takes the
  same two supersession shapes `proc-v14` took
  ([process-version.md](process-version.md#freezing-the-cutover-procedure)):
  each predictor's open `proc-v14` window **closes** at this label's instant
  and a `proc-v15` window opens there for each new digest, and the three
  judges' blessings are replaced. Nothing is de-counted and nothing is
  re-owed. Until the carrying merge stamps the six new blessings, the carried
  bless map is empty while `FROZEN_SINCE` stays at `proc-v14`'s instant, so
  every board built in that interval counts nothing of this label.

  **What moved, in what every cell reads.**
  - *The instruction files.* Every cell was told to read `AGENTS.md` first,
    and Claude Code and Codex load `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` from the tree
    on their own, so every cell answered under instructions no digest hashed.
    The predict, evaluate and labeling prompts now open with a short *Cell
    contract* (the lane, the harness-owned fields, the leakage clock, no
    secrets, `flags.json` as the channel, validation) and name no other
    instruction file. The kickoff lines name only the actor's template. Every
    job that starts an engine in a checkout — run-predict, run-evaluate,
    run-backtest, the run-analytics labeler and integration-test's scenario
    and labeler-smoke jobs — marks the two files and the `.claude/` reviewer
    subagents skip-worktree and deletes them before its first engine step. `tests/test_cell_instructions.py`
    holds all three. The labeling prompt is in no registered digest
    ([qp-topic.md](qp-topic.md)), so its edit moves no registration.
  - *PDFs and installs.* `fedcourts pdf-text <file>` prints a PDF's text
    through the corpus's own pypdf extractor, and both prompts name it. Package
    installs are refused in each engine's own surface, from one prefix list
    (`fedcourtsai.cell_policy`, `fedcourts cell-policy`): claude-code
    `permissions.deny` rules, codex `forbidden` execpolicy rules in the codex
    account's `$CODEX_HOME/rules/` (a leg running a real turn fails without
    them, and checks them with the pinned CLI's `execpolicy check` before
    the turn), gemini a `run_shell_command` deny rule through `policyPaths`.
    It refuses command prefixes the engine parses, not
    outcomes ([security.md](security.md)). The back-test and local cells
    launched by `pipeline/runner.py` do not carry it. Both prompts drop the
    line saying a bare `fedcourts` is not on the shell's `PATH`, which the
    `agent-shell-fedcourts-on-path` boundary made untrue for the live cells.
  - *The frozen cert anchor, named.* The predict prompt names
    `record/context.json`'s `cert_anchor` and its three keys — `rate`, pooled
    over the cell's band, under its `salience_version`, from Terms strictly
    before its own, out of the statpack in force at placement;
    `statpack_digest`; `lookback_terms` — as the baseline
    its cert skill is scored against, and says what a null `rate` and a null
    record mean.
  - *The same-question list.* `provision.SAME_QUESTION_WITHHELD` is off: a
    forward cert cell's provisioning stages `record/same-question.json`,
    other petitions whose questions presented read like this one's, by
    text-similarity score, with each one's status at the cutoff, and the
    predict prompt says how to read it.

  **What the harness releases with this label.**
  - *The pinned cert anchor.* `PINNED_CERT_ANCHOR_FROM` names `proc-v15`, the
    label registered here: a cert grading stamped under it whose scored
    prediction froze `context.cert_anchor` stamps that anchor, once verified
    against the predict cell's run id, `main`'s first-parent statpack history
    (read from a bare clone made after the judge's step) and
    `config/tracking.yaml`, instead of pooling the statpack checked out at
    grading ([process-version.md](process-version.md)). The anchor must name
    the build in force at the run id, or the one it replaced where that build
    landed within `CHECKOUT_SLACK` (six hours) before it, since a cell checks
    out its trigger commit before the run id is minted. A grading of a cell
    placed without the record still pools at grading. This moves who fixes
    the baseline's build, not the quantity: the same pooler over the same
    frozen context.
  - *The same-question boundary.* `cert-same-question-list` is registered
    **pending** by the merged switch-on (every predictor, reach `all`, not
    gradual); `promotion-record` stamps it at this label's carrying merge. It
    coincides with this label's window edge, since the same merge moves every
    predictor digest.
  - *No other boundary.* The instruction-file removal, `pdf-text` and the
    install refusal change what a cell reads or can run, but they land in the
    same merge that moves every predictor and evaluator digest, so the label's
    own window edge is their boundary and none is registered for them.

  **What scored figures move.** None at once: no rate, membership rule or
  scoring rule moves for a committed grading. From this label's gradings on,
  a cert cell placed after the anchor record carries its placement-time
  baseline, so a cert skill figure that spans the label pools two baseline
  rules; such a figure reads per label.

- **`sal-v6` registered, inactive, and `sal-v5` never to be activated;
  recorded 2026-10-30.** No freeze commit belongs to this entry, on the
  `sal-v4` registration's pattern: the salience version sits outside the
  process digest (`pipeline_sha` is not an input), carries its own
  data-visible boundary (`context.salience_version`), and a registration
  re-blesses nothing. `uv run fedcourts process-digest --all` prints the same
  six `proc-v15` digests before and after this change. Carried to `main` by
  the promotion tagged `promotion/2026-10-30-2` (merge commit
  `d1fea1be5dbf3bc923038e0e98dbbfac26c0d629`, merged `2026-10-30T21:35:48Z`).

  **What `sal-v6` is.** `sal-v5`'s call-for-response relist count
  (`call_for_response_superseded`, over `distributed_after_call`) and its Rule
  20 writ scope (`opening_writ`, `SalienceScorer.admits`), read as the same
  callables, over `sal-v3`'s `caption-v2` band, carve-in and reachable ladder,
  with `sal-v4`'s `dist-v2` parse pin, cutpoints, band vocabulary and arrival
  draw. `SALIENCE_VERSION` stays `sal-v4`, so nothing the live pass selects,
  latches or stamps moves; `statpack.json` and `salience-replay.json` carry a
  sixth version's bands from their next render.

  **Why `sal-v5` is set aside.** Its `caption-v3` petitioner class reads the
  Solicitor General's office as petitioner-side counsel, and that reading
  carries post-outcome information. The Clerk lists a United States amicus
  supporting petitioners under "Petitioner", so the side guard, which drops
  only `other`-role counsel, admits a post-grant amicus; and every stored
  snapshot of the historical rows postdates their grants, so no stored record
  dates the entry before the outcome. Of the 16 resolved rows `caption-v3`
  moves to `federal`, at least 5 (all granted) carry post-outcome
  information: 19-1257 and 25-840 by a post-grant United States amicus listed
  on the petitioner side (25-840 observed directly: no office on the
  petitioner side in the snapshots of 2026-07-12 through 2026-08-16, after its
  2026-06-29 grant, and the office present from 2026-10-04, after the amicus
  brief of 2026-09-15), and 18-1587, 24-20 and 24-422 by consolidation with a
  government petition in the grant order itself. No stored snapshot of the
  other historical moved rows predates its grant, so they cannot be dated.
  `sal-v5` stays registered, so a pool or replay cell published under its
  label still replays, and it is never activated.

  **The relist rule against the census's reading, measured.** The frame is
  the census's: the 12,168 resolved live-slice rows in the scored segment with
  docket Terms 2017–2024, read after the `salience-cert-backfill` apply, of
  which 1,470 carry a call for response. On all 1,470 the back-filled
  `call_for_response_at`, `distributed_after_call` and `distribution_count`
  each match a fresh reading of the row's newest live snapshot. The census
  stored no per-row `s`, so its reading was reconstructed from each
  snapshot's dated distributions: the first distribution filed on or before
  the call with its conference not yet sat, and a distribution after the call
  naming a conference not named before it. Per Term, under that reading:

  | Term | rows with a call | rule `s = 1` | census `s = 1` | agree | disagreeing ids |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 2017 | 203 | 191 | 191 | 203 | — |
  | 2018 | 185 | 179 | 178 | 184 | 18-1078 |
  | 2019 | 184 | 181 | 181 | 184 | — |
  | 2020 | 205 | 201 | 199 | 203 | 20-1737, 20-791 |
  | 2021 | 173 | 166 | 165 | 172 | 21-1241 |
  | 2022 | 161 | 156 | 156 | 161 | — |
  | 2023 | 170 | 158 | 158 | 170 | — |
  | 2024 | 189 | 185 | 184 | 188 | 24-1192 |
  | all | 1,470 | 1,417 | 1,412 | 1,465 (99.66%) | 5 |

  Read instead off the conference pending at the call, the two agree on
  1,468. Every disagreement has the rule reading `s = 1` and is definitional:
  a call dated after the first conference sat (20-1737, 20-791), or a call
  following a relist or a reschedule (18-1078, 21-1241, 24-1192). None comes
  from an unfilled column or a call-date or count mismatch, and none is a
  Rule 20 writ.

  The figures are on production index blob `d6086761…aa18703a` (newest pull
  2026-10-30, newest stored snapshot row 2026-07-13).

- **`sal-v6` activated, and a refused band carries its reason; recorded
  2026-10-31.** A distinct entry from the 2026-10-30 registration entry above,
  on the `sal-v4` activation's pattern: that entry is landed, and its only
  editable content was its own promotion placeholders. No freeze commit
  belongs to this entry: the salience version sits outside the process digest
  (`pipeline_sha` is not an input), carries its own data-visible boundary
  (`context.salience_version`), and a flip re-blesses nothing. `uv run
  fedcourts process-digest --all` prints the same six `proc-v15` digests
  before and after this change.

  **The flip is one constant.** `SALIENCE_VERSION` goes `sal-v4` → `sal-v6`.
  `sal-v6` pins `dist-v2`, which `cert_signals.DEFAULT_DISTRIBUTION_PARSE`
  already names, so the pairing `sal-v4`'s activation needed does not arise
  and the stored `distribution_count` column needs no re-derivation. Nothing
  in `src/` branches on the literal: the live pass, the corpus stamp, the
  frozen cell band, the statpack's `segments`/`alt_segments` split, the gate
  replay's ordering and `segment-anchors`' default follow the constant. Two
  inputs `sal-v6` reads beyond `sal-v4`'s, `distributed_after_call` and
  `opening_writ`, are filled on the decided rows by the
  `salience-cert-backfill` apply (29,503 fills; the control dry run reports
  0) on blob `d6086761…aa18703a`, and the live poll latches both at ingest.

  **What it moves.** The live pass scores, latches and stamps under `sal-v6`.
  A petition distributed again after a call for response loses the relist
  that distribution read as; a Rule 20 writ leaves the scored segment and is
  neither scored nor latched. The pass stamps such a row with `sal-v6` and no
  score, so the gate reads it as deferred rather than failing open into the
  predict scope as an unscored row would, and the `sal-v4` score the corpus
  column held on it is cleared; one already latched keeps its latch, which is
  one-way. A cohort's capacity counts no existing latch, so the first `sal-v6`
  pass latches each pending conference's `sal-v6` top-N beside the `sal-v4`
  latches already there: the conferences pending at the flip fund more
  petitions than either version alone would, once. The size is the
  `newly_selected` count of `uv run fedcourts reconcile-salience-selection`, a
  dry run read before the promotion. `unlatch-overselected` would de-select
  pending petitions the new rule demotes; it is not part of activation and is
  not run. The scored
  window opens at the first post-promotion metrics refresh, as for every
  earlier flip. A cell minted before it pools a `sal-v6` anchor from the
  committed `alt_segments` block, but reads `statpack.md`'s `sal-v4` table
  as a version mismatch.

  **The post-back-fill pack.** The metrics refresh merged to `main` as
  `648fc4355` rendered `metrics/statpack.json` from a commit whose corpus
  pointer names blob `ffc504df…62d8`, which descends from the back-fill's
  `d6086761…`. Its Terms stamp `sal-v4` and
  carry a `sal-v6` block in `alt_segments`. Pooled through the scorer's own
  pooler over the complete Terms OT2017–OT2024 (the anchor for an OT2025
  docket, lookback 10; grant-family rate, resolved `n`, unweighted on this
  frame), by `uv run fedcourts segment-anchors --term 2025 --salience-version
  <v> --statpack <that pack>`:

  | band | `sal-v6` terminal | `sal-v6` risk-set | `sal-v4` terminal | `sal-v4` risk-set |
  | --- | --: | --: | --: | --: |
  | federal | 75.98% (136/179) | 75.98% (n=179) | 75.82% (138/182) | 75.82% (n=182) |
  | high | 34.55% (246/712) | 34.55% (n=712) | 35.44% (319/900) | 35.44% (n=900) |
  | state | 18.56% (54/291) | 22.82% (n=390) | 16.97% (47/277) | 22.82% (n=390) |
  | elevated | 20.48% (250/1,221) | 25.14% (n=1,834) | 10.50% (213/2,029) | 17.40% (n=2,816) |
  | baseline | 1.50% (143/9,539) | 5.31% (n=11,373) | 1.30% (114/8,780) | 5.21% (n=11,596) |

  The frames are 11,942 resolved rows under `sal-v6` against 12,168 under
  `sal-v4`, the 12,168 the registration entry's census frame counts; the 226
  rows `sal-v6` leaves out are the writs, carrying 2 grant-family outcomes
  (829 against 831 over the two frames). Per Term, `sal-v6`'s `elevated`
  terminal rate is above `sal-v4`'s in all eight complete Terms (14.7% to
  25.3% against 7.8% to 13.1%), on 127 to 184 resolved rows a Term against
  207 to 295; `high` moves both ways (lower in four Terms, higher in four).
  So the call-for-response rule takes out of `elevated` and `high` the rows
  whose second distribution was not a relist, and `elevated` separates more
  sharply from `baseline` (13.7× against 8.1× on the terminal rates) while
  `high` separates a little less (23.0× against 27.3×). These are
  per-band composition figures, the bar `sal-v3`'s activation read off a
  census; they are not a selection comparison.

  **The replay reading.** The prerequisite reads a cross-version comparison
  at matched recall, which is `salience-replay`'s. The salience-gate replay
  over OT2017–OT2024 (run-backtest run 41155571013, 2026-10-31, retrospective
  stratum, its `metrics/salience-replay.json` carried by the run's own PR)
  reads, pooled over the eight Terms:

  | policy | version | eligible | selected | grants caught / realized | recall | precision |
  | --- | --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
  | resolution | `sal-v4` | 12,168 | 4,309 | 699 / 831 | 84.1% | 16.2% |
  | resolution | `sal-v6` | 11,942 | 4,178 | 690 / 829 | 83.2% | 16.5% |
  | distribution-1 | `sal-v4` | 12,168 | 3,253 | 376 / 831 | 45.2% | 11.6% |
  | distribution-1 | `sal-v6` | 11,942 | 3,253 | 376 / 829 | 45.4% | 11.6% |

  The two versions do not sit at one recall, so the reading is the margin
  between them. At `resolution`, the 131 petitions `sal-v4` selects beyond
  `sal-v6` carry 9 grants, 6.9%, which is the eligible frame's own grant
  rate (831 of 12,168, 6.8%): what `sal-v6` gives up it gives up at the rate
  of an unranked pick. Per Term, `sal-v6` catches more grants in four Terms,
  fewer in three and the same in one, on fewer selections in every Term. At
  `distribution-1` the selections and grants caught are the same; recall
  differs only by the two writ grants leaving the denominator. `sal-v5`'s
  cells equal `sal-v6`'s, because the replay's projection carries no counsel
  and so cannot show the `caption-v3` difference. The `arrival` policy
  selects no row under any version and reads nothing here. On this reading
  `sal-v6` ranks no worse than `sal-v4`: the replay finds no selection cost
  to the flip, and no gain beyond the margin above.

  **A refused band carries its reason.** `PredictionContext` gains
  `band_refused`, `"outside-segment"` where the band freeze refuses a row the
  active scorer's segment leaves out, null everywhere else (a frozen band, an
  unobservable docket, an application docket, and every earlier context).
  Such a cell freezes `band` and `salience_version` null with
  `signals_observable` true, which before this field a reader could tell from
  an unobservable docket only by that flag. Under `sal-v6` the field is set
  only on a cert cell whose payload's opening petition entry is a Rule 20
  writ. The cell reads `record/context.json`, so the field joins its
  information set; it adds nothing the cell could not read, since the
  opening entry is in the staged snapshot. No prompt text or other digest
  input changes, so no digest moves; the predict prompt describes `band`'s
  null cases and does not yet name the field, which is left for the next
  re-bless. The boundary is `context-band-refused`, every predictor, reach
  `all`, not gradual: every cell provisioned after the carrying merge freezes
  the key. It is registered **pending** in this change
  (`fedcourts register-boundary`), stamped by the promotion record. It is
  composition, not a cut; no board reads the field.

  Carried to `main` by the promotion tagged `promotion/2026-10-31` (merge
  commit `36071d617fb0bd8c5fed990422f5e3b5bdd6e286`, merged `2026-10-31T13:36:41Z`).

  The runnable effect check once it is live:
  - on `main`, `uv run python -c "from fedcourtsai.pipeline.salience import
    SALIENCE_VERSION; print(SALIENCE_VERSION)"` prints `sal-v6`;
  - after the first post-promotion metrics refresh, `jq -r
    '.terms[].salience_version' metrics/statpack.json | sort -u` prints
    `sal-v6`, every Term's `alt_segments` holds a `sal-v4` block, and
    `elevated`'s published OT2017–OT2024 terminal rate reads near 20%, not
    near 10%; a refresh leaving it near 10% is evidence the flip is not live;
  - on the first predict run's collect PR after the carrying merge, `jq -c
    '[.context.salience_version, .context | has("band_refused")]'
    data/cases/scotus/*/events/*/predictions/*/<run_id>/prediction.json`
    prints `"sal-v6"` (or null on an unbanded cell) and `true` for every
    file;
  - `uv run python -c "from fedcourtsai.process_version import
    HARNESS_BOUNDARIES as H; print('context-band-refused' in {b.name for b
    in H})"` prints `True` once the promotion record has stamped the row.

- **A multi-respondent opposition is cut brief by brief at a cell's cutoff;
  recorded 2026-10-31.** No freeze commit belongs to this entry: no prompt
  text or other digest input changes, and `uv run fedcourts process-digest
  --all` prints the same six `proc-v15` digests before and after this change.

  **What changes.** The `brief-in-opposition` row combines every respondent's
  brief under one header each, the header naming that brief's docket date,
  and the row is dated by its earliest brief. `provision.documents_before`
  placed it whole by that date, so a cell placed between two respondents'
  briefs read the later one as well. It now places each brief by its own
  header date (an undated header on the row's `fetched_at`) and stages only
  the briefs filed before the cutoff. A cut row's manifest fields describe the
  kept briefs alone: `entry_date` the earliest kept brief's, `url` the stored
  links whose entries on the served docket fall before the cutoff, `truncated` whether a
  kept brief carries a cut note, and `pages` the row's count scaled by the
  share of text kept. A row no later brief reaches is staged byte for byte as
  before. A row stored under the older latest-brief dating, which a cell
  between its briefs used to lose whole, now gives that cell its earlier
  briefs.

  **Why.** The call-for-response moment's cutoff falls just after the Court
  calls for a response, so in a case where one respondent opposed early and
  another waived, the brief filed after the cutoff is the called-for response
  itself. On the committed ledger at this change, 3 of the 628 cells placed
  at a cutoff read a brief filed on or after it: the three call-for-response
  cells of scotus/73538544 in run `20261029T180303Z`, which read a
  co-respondent's response filed 2026-10-13 against a 2026-09-11 cutoff. Of
  the 158 cases those 628 cells sit on, 65 hold an opposition row and 8 of
  those combine more than one brief. Figures on production index blob
  `af21a39e…a711c6a8` (newest pull 2026-10-31, newest stored snapshot row
  2026-07-13), the per-case content store read the same day.

  The boundary is `opposition-cut-by-brief`, every predictor, reach `all`, not
  gradual: every cell provisioned after the carrying merge is cut this way.
  It is registered **pending** in this change (`fedcourts
  register-boundary`), stamped by the promotion record. No board reads it as a
  cut: the 3 cells it would split are one event's, too few to read a side.

  Carried to `main` by the promotion tagged `<FILL: promotion tag>` (merge
  commit `<FILL: merge sha>`, merged `<FILL: merged time utc>`).

  The runnable effect check once it is live:

    HARNESS_BOUNDARIES as H; print('opposition-cut-by-brief' in {b.name for
    b in H})"` prints `True` once the promotion record has stamped the row;
  - where the corpus is pulled, `uv run fedcourts provision-snapshot --court
    scotus --docket 73538544 --event evt-order-call-for-response-disposition

- **`proc-v16`: the forecast document is graded on every stage, cert and
  merits cells read the decision below, and the predict prompt names a refused
  band; recorded 2026-10-31.** Carried to `main` by the promotion tagged
  `<FILL: promotion tag>` (merge commit `<FILL: merge sha>`, merged
  `<FILL: merged time utc>`), to be tagged **`prereg/proc-v16`**. Registered
  under the merge-stamped rule, so its counting instant, its six bless moments
  and every window edge it moves are the carrying merge's committer time. Both
  prompts change, so it takes the two supersession shapes `proc-v15` took
  ([process-version.md](process-version.md#freezing-the-cutover-procedure)):
  each predictor's open `proc-v15` window **closes** at this label's instant
  and a `proc-v16` window opens there for each new digest, and the three
  judges' blessings are replaced. Nothing is de-counted. Until the carrying
  merge stamps the six new blessings, the carried bless map is empty while
  `FROZEN_SINCE` stays at `proc-v15`'s instant, so every board built in that
  interval counts nothing of this label.

  **What moved, in what every cell reads.**
  - *The forecast document's grade, `predicted_reasoning_quality`.* The
    evaluate prompt gains a *Grading the forecast document* section: every
    judge grades each candidate's `predicted_reasoning.md` on every stage, 0
    to 1 on the anchored rubric, with the three to five central claims the
    grade rests on (`predicted_reasoning_review`), or a null with the
    record's ground for it. The rubric, its anchors, the central-claims list,
    the null rule and the rule that the vote weighs less than the disposition
    and the ground are the pilot section's at sha256
    `3f03b9f2cf067d1bbb07fd681dcdacf47a649a4364cace605130eb73c1b31ce1`,
    reframed as a registered section; the prompt's instruction not to grade
    the forecast document becomes an instruction to grade it only in those
    two fields, so `reasoning_quality` still grades `reasoning.md` alone. A
    candidate with no forecast document gets neither field. `validate` takes
    a committed grade only from an evaluator digest blessed at this label or
    later, and refuses one under an earlier or unstamped digest
    (`predicted_reasoning_grade_only_under_a_prompt_that_asks`,
    `PREDICTED_REASONING_GRADE_FROM`). The design is
    *Grading the forecast document, design* in
    [outcome-decomposition.md](outcome-decomposition.md), whose register now
    routes the document to this grade.
  - *Every writing of the decision, on every evaluate cell.* run-evaluate's
    opinion step passes `provision-opinion --writings` on every row, so a
    merits cell stages each concurrence and dissent beside the majority, as
    the grade's check of who writes separately needs. It changes the
    information set of every judge-authored reading, not only this grade's.
    The writings are staged on cert and interim evaluate cells too, so a cert
    or interim cell graded after the case's merits decision sees merits
    writings that one graded before it does not. The prompt limits their use
    to what the document forecast a decision would hold, but cert and interim
    readings can differ by grading date.
  - *The decision below, for cert and merits cells.* The `decision-below` and
    `lower-court-docket` kinds leave `provision.WITHHELD_KINDS` and are staged
    for cert-stage and merits-stage cells only
    (`provision.LOWER_COURT_STAGES`), never interim: the maintainer's choice,
    2026-10-31, since an interim application comes from a court the fill does
    not join. The predict prompt names both files, says they come from a
    CourtListener match by the lower court's docket number rather than the
    Court's record, and says a missing file means no match was stored, never
    that there was no decision below. The fill
    (`fedcourts enrich-decision-below`, in `run-pull`'s live job) reaches
    cases on a rotation, cases the ledger forecasts and the salience selection
    first, then never-attempted before stale, so the share of cells holding
    the files grows window by window rather than at the merge. The merits
    back-test replay sweep stages neither kind, because the fill walks
    undecided cases only and a decided case holds them by accident of timing;
    the case-summary plan reads neither.
  - *A refused band, named.* The predict prompt's description of `band`'s
    null cases names `context.band_refused`: `"outside-segment"` where the
    active salience version's segment leaves the docket out, so `band` and
    `salience_version` are null although the snapshot was readable. The
    field and its `context-band-refused` boundary were registered by the
    `sal-v6` activation entry, which left the prompt sentence for this
    re-bless.

  **What the harness releases with this label.**
  - *The decision-below boundary.* `decision-below-documents` is registered
    **pending** by the change that stages the two kinds (every predictor,
    reach `all`, `gradual`, since the files reach cases by back-fill);
    `promotion-record` stamps it at this label's carrying merge, so it
    coincides with this label's window edge. `context-band-refused` is not
    this batch's: it was registered with `sal-v6`'s activation and is
    stamped by the promotion that carries that change.
  - *The pilot note.* run-evaluate's `reasoning-pilot` and
    `reasoning-pilot-merits` rounds stay: they re-grade a fixed sample under
    the registered prompt and upload rather than commit. The pilot file
    (`.github/prompts/pilot/predicted-reasoning-quality.md`) carries no
    rubric; it marks the round and changes no instruction, and the round's
    report hashes the evaluate prompt.

  **The pilot evidence.** Two merits calibration rounds,
  `20261026T100615Z` and `20261028T144848Z`, graded the replay merits
  calibration cells against the maintainer's hand labels on all 15 sampled
  documents (label sheet sha256
  `d51670c53fbf79300f8e0335129ca17f32637110dc7e8032df1a0c9deac9ddd0`, sample
  sha256 `62eb08a3299ebaf9511344c3d581a9592e982d08d5ac5fd7fbb1c6c1b0e477af`);
  the first graded under the section at sha256
  `8ce6bbdea09771a503734847326163e2a5bbe5712977f53df12fbae81be3236d`, the
  second under the section at sha256
  `3f03b9f2cf067d1bbb07fd681dcdacf47a649a4364cace605130eb73c1b31ce1`, whose
  rubric is the one registered here. The maintainer read the second round's regrade
  on 2026-10-28 and accepted it as reasonable. The reading is the one *The
  pilot, and what it reports* fixes: the labels are a reference, not ground
  truth, and the judges are not required to match the maintainer exactly.

  **What scored figures move.** None. The grade is collected, not published:
  no board, summary or site page reads it, and it enters no claim total, no
  rank key and no other grade. Publishing it, per stage, per process version
  and per rubric, with its agreement figures beside every mean, is a later
  change with its own site change. Every judge-authored reading
  (`reasoning_quality`, `big_case`, the leakage grading, the semantic
  grades) starts a new rubric signature at this label, and series that span
  it read per rubric ([metrics/README.md](../metrics/README.md)).

  **The back-grade, not yet owed by anything.** The registration says the
  already-resolved forward documents are graded once, in new evaluation runs
  stamped with this label; committed evaluations are never edited. The
  backlog does not owe those runs: its idempotency gate
  (`matrix.event_has_evaluations`) asks whether a judge has graded the event,
  under any digest. At `origin/main` `7546878f3`, 198 resolved events carry a
  committed prediction; 194 of them (147 cert, 47 interim) carry 579 latest
  forward predictions with a forecast document, and every one of the 194 is
  graded by all three judges, so the backlog would mint 0 cells for them, and
  never will. A back-grade is 582 (judge × event) cells, and no lane offers
  it: run-evaluate's dispatch input picks a derivation, never a case, and
  only the pilot derivations pass `--force`, whose output is uploaded, not
  committed. Running it needs a new run-evaluate derivation, a workflow
  change not built here.

  Committing such a back-grade would re-score committed boards. Each of its
  evaluations becomes its cell's latest grading
  (`integrity.latest_evaluation_runs`), so it re-decides `leakage_suspected`,
  which `store.stratify` reads to drop a cell from every rank key and scored
  aggregate; it re-stamps `segment_base_rate`, `brier_skill_score` and
  `claim_scores` against the statpack checked out at back-grade time on
  every cell whose prediction froze no `cert_anchor`, which is every cell
  placed before `proc-v15`; and the retiring digests' per-rubric readings
  lose those cells. Whether the back-grade is a committed round at all, or a
  cheaper route — an uploaded pilot-style round, or a grade-only evaluation
  the latest-grading collapse skips for every other field — is an open
  design question, as is whether and when to spend on it.

  The runnable effect check once it is live:
  - `uv run python -c "from fedcourtsai.process_version import
    CURRENT_PROCESS_LABEL as L; from fedcourtsai.validate import
    PREDICTED_REASONING_GRADE_FROM as R; print(L, R)"` prints
    `proc-v16 proc-v16`, and `uv run fedcourts process-digest --all` prints the
    six digests above;
  - on the first evaluate run's collect PR after the carrying merge, `jq -c
    '[.process_version.label, .predicted_reasoning_quality,
    (.predicted_reasoning_review.central_claims | length)]'
    data/cases/scotus/*/events/*/evaluations/*/*/<run_id>/evaluation.json`
    prints `"proc-v16"` and, for every candidate with a forecast document, a
    number with 3 to 5 claims or a null beside a `not_gradeable` ground; each
    merits cell's job log shows `provision-opinion` staging its writings
    where the corpus stores them;
  - on the first predict run after the carrying merge, a forward cert or
    merits cell on a case the fill has reached carries
    `record/documents/decision-below.txt`, and no interim cell carries
    either lower-court file;
  - on `main`, `uv run python -c "from fedcourtsai.process_version import
    HARNESS_BOUNDARIES as H; n = {b.name for b in H};
    print({'decision-below-documents', 'context-band-refused'} <= n)"` prints
